Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
Coulomb's pairwise interaction obeys the principle of linear superposition, while the total force in a dielectric medium incorporates the opposing fields of induced polarization charges.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
The principle of superposition explicitly states that the mutual interaction force between two isolated point charges is independent of any third or additional charges present in the assembly. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
In a dielectric medium, the net electrostatic force between two charges is reduced because the dielectric undergoes polarization, creating induced charges that oppose the original electric field: \(F_{\text{med}} = \frac{F_{\text{vac}}}{\varepsilon_r}\). Since \(\varepsilon_r > 1\), the net force decreases by a factor of \(\varepsilon_r\), rather than increasing. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion:
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत:
कूलॉम बल अध्यारोपण के सिद्धांत का पालन करता है, जबकि परावैद्युत माध्यम में प्रेरित ध्रुवण आवेशों के कारण नेट बल परिवर्तित होता है।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
अध्यारोपण का सिद्धांत स्पष्ट रूप से बताता है कि दो आवेशों के बीच लगने वाला पारस्परिक कूलॉम बल किसी तीसरे या अन्य आवेशों की उपस्थिति से प्रभावित नहीं होता है। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
परावैद्युत माध्यम में माध्यम के ध्रुवण के कारण नेट स्थिरवैद्युत बल घट जाता है: \(F_{\text{med}} = \frac{F_{\text{vac}}}{\varepsilon_r}\)। चूँकि \(\varepsilon_r > 1\) होता है, अतः बल \(\varepsilon_r\) गुना कम होता है, न कि बढ़ता है। अतः कथन II गलत है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
कथन I सही है परंतु कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRICCHARGESANDFIELDS_STATEMENT_Q04 - Electrostatic field line geometry and work done along closed paths

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In an electrostatic field, two field lines can intersect each other at points where the electric field strength reaches a local maximum.

Statement II: Because the electrostatic field is conservative, the work done by the electrostatic force in moving a test charge around any closed path is zero.

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: स्थिरवैद्युत क्षेत्र में, दो क्षेत्र रेखाएं उन बिंदुओं पर एक-दूसरे को प्रतिच्छेद कर सकती हैं जहाँ विद्युत क्षेत्र की तीव्रता स्थानीय अधिकतम तक पहुँचती है।

कथन II: चूँकि स्थिरवैद्युत क्षेत्र संरक्षी होता है, इसलिए किसी परीक्षण आवेश को किसी बंद पथ के अनुदिश ले जाने में स्थिरवैद्युत बल द्वारा किया गया कार्य शून्य होता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
Electric field lines map the direction of the net electric field vector, and conservative fields satisfy the zero circulation condition \(\oint \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{l} = 0\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
The tangent to an electric field line at any point gives the unique direction of the net electric field vector. If two field lines were to cross, there would be two distinct tangents at the single point of intersection, implying two simultaneous directions for the net electric field, which is physically impossible. Field lines never intersect under any circumstances. Therefore, Statement I is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
The electrostatic force is a central, conservative force derivable from a scalar electric potential. Consequently, the line integral of the electric field around any closed loop is identically zero (\(\oint \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{l} = 0\)), meaning the work done around any closed path is zero. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion:
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत:
विद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाएं कुल विद्युत क्षेत्र सदिश की दिशा को निरूपित करती हैं, और संरक्षी क्षेत्रों में किसी बंद पथ पर रेखा समाकलन \(\oint \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{l} = 0\) होता है।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
किसी बिंदु पर विद्युत क्षेत्र रेखा पर खींची गई स्पर्श रेखा उस बिंदु पर परिणामी विद्युत क्षेत्र की दिशा बताती है। यदि दो रेखाएं प्रतिच्छेद करेंगी, तो प्रतिच्छेद बिंदु पर दो स्पर्श रेखाएं होंगी, जिसका अर्थ होगा कि एक ही बिंदु पर क्षेत्र की दो दिशाएं हैं, जो भौतिक रूप से असंभव है। अतः क्षेत्र रेखाएं कभी नहीं काटती हैं। अतः कथन I गलत है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
स्थिरवैद्युत बल पूर्णतः संरक्षी होता है। अतः किसी भी बंद पथ के अनुदिश किसी परीक्षण आवेश को चलाने में स्थिरवैद्युत बल द्वारा किया गया कुल कार्य सदैव शून्य होता है। अतः कथन II सही है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
कथन I गलत है परंतु कथन II सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRICCHARGESANDFIELDS_STATEMENT_Q05 - Electric flux dependence on enclosed charge and surface shape

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The net electric flux passing through a closed Gaussian surface depends entirely on the net enclosed charge and is independent of the size and geometric shape of the surface.

Statement II: If the net electric flux through a closed surface is zero, the net charge enclosed within the surface must be zero, although the electric field on the surface itself need not be zero.

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: किसी बंद गाउसीय पृष्ठ से गुजरने वाला कुल विद्युत फ्लक्स पूर्णतः उसके भीतर परिबद्ध नेट आवेश पर निर्भर करता है तथा पृष्ठ के आकार और ज्यामितीय आकृति से स्वतंत्र होता है।

कथन II: यदि किसी बंद पृष्ठ से गुजरने वाला कुल विद्युत फ्लक्स शून्य है, तो पृष्ठ के भीतर परिबद्ध नेट आवेश शून्य होना अनिवार्य है, यद्यपि पृष्ठ पर स्वयं विद्युत क्षेत्र का शून्य होना आवश्यक नहीं है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
Gauss's law states that the net outward electric flux through any closed surface \(S\) is given by \(\Phi = \oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{A} = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
Gauss's law applies to any closed surface regardless of its geometric form, whether it is a sphere, cylinder, cube, or irregular shape. Expanding or shrinking the surface does not change the total number of electric field lines crossing it, provided the enclosed charge remains unchanged. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
By Gauss's law, \(\Phi = 0 \implies q_{\text{enclosed}} = 0\). However, electric charges lying outside the surface can produce a non-zero electric field at points on the surface, where field lines enter at one side and exit at another. Thus, \(\mathbf{E}\) on the surface can be non-zero even while the integral flux is zero. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion:
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत:
गाउस के नियमानुसार किसी बंद पृष्ठ \(S\) से निर्गत कुल विद्युत फ्लक्स \(\Phi = \oint_S \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{A} = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}\) होता है।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
गाउस का नियम किसी भी आकार या आकृति के बंद पृष्ठ के लिए सत्य है। जब तक भीतर परिबद्ध आवेश नहीं बदलता, पृष्ठ को छोटा या बड़ा करने पर उससे गुजरने वाला कुल फ्लक्स अपरिवर्तित रहता है। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
यदि कुल फ्लक्स \(\Phi = 0\) है, तो गाउस के नियम से परिबद्ध नेट आवेश \(q_{\text{enclosed}} = 0\) होना आवश्यक है। बाह्य आवेशों की उपस्थिति के कारण पृष्ठ के विभिन्न बिंदुओं पर विद्युत क्षेत्र \(\mathbf{E} \neq 0\) हो सकता है (जितनी क्षेत्र रेखाएं प्रवेश करती हैं, उतनी ही बाहर निकल जाती हैं)। अतः कथन II सही है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
कथन I और कथन II दोनों सही हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRICCHARGESANDFIELDS_STATEMENT_Q06 - Dipole in uniform and non-uniform fields

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: An electric dipole placed in a uniform external electric field experiences both a non-zero net translatory force and a non-zero net torque for all orientations.

Statement II: When an electric dipole is aligned parallel to a non-uniform electric field whose magnitude increases along the direction of the dipole moment, the net force on the dipole is directed opposite to the field gradient.

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एकसमान बाह्य विद्युत क्षेत्र में रखा गया विद्युत द्विध्रुव सभी अभिविन्यासों के लिए एक अशून्य कुल स्थानांतरीय बल तथा एक अशून्य कुल बल-आघूर्ण दोनों का अनुभव करता है।

कथन II: जब एक विद्युत द्विध्रुव को किसी ऐसे असमान विद्युत क्षेत्र के समानांतर रखा जाता है जिसका परिमाण द्विध्रुव आघूर्ण की दिशा में बढ़ता है, तो द्विध्रुव पर नेट बल क्षेत्र प्रवणता के विपरीत दिशा में होता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
The behavior of an electric dipole of moment \(\mathbf{p}\) in an external field \(\mathbf{E}\) is governed by \(\mathbf{F}_{\text{net}} = \sum q_i \mathbf{E}(\mathbf{r}_i)\) and \(\boldsymbol{\tau} = \mathbf{p} \times \mathbf{E}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
In a uniform electric field, the force on \(+q\) is \(+q\mathbf{E}\) and the force on \(-q\) is \(-q\mathbf{E}\). The vector sum is identically zero (\(\mathbf{F}_{\text{net}} = 0\)) for every orientation. Furthermore, when the dipole is aligned parallel or antiparallel to the field (\(\theta = 0^\circ\) or \(180^\circ\)), the torque \(\tau = pE\sin\theta\) is also zero. Therefore, Statement I is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
When \(\mathbf{p}\) is parallel to \(\mathbf{E}\), the positive charge \(+q\) is located further in the direction of the field where the field magnitude is greater (\(E_+ > E_-\)). Consequently, the forward force on \(+q\) exceeds the backward force on \(-q\), resulting in a net force in the direction of increasing field (along the field gradient), not opposite to it. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion:
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत:
विद्युत क्षेत्र \(\mathbf{E}\) में द्विध्रुव \(\mathbf{p}\) पर कुल बल \(\mathbf{F}_{\text{net}} = \sum q_i \mathbf{E}\) तथा बल-आघूर्ण \(\boldsymbol{\tau} = \mathbf{p} \times \mathbf{E}\) द्वारा निर्धारित होता है।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
एकसमान विद्युत क्षेत्र में दोनों आवेशों पर लगने वाले बल समान और विपरीत होते हैं, अतः नेट स्थानांतरीय बल सदैव शून्य होता है। इसके अतिरिक्त, \(\theta = 0^\circ\) या \(180^\circ\) पर बल-आघूर्ण भी शून्य होता है। अतः कथन I गलत है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
जब \(\mathbf{p}\) और \(\mathbf{E}\) समानांतर होते हैं और क्षेत्र द्विध्रुव की दिशा में बढ़ रहा होता है, तो धनावेश \(+q\) अधिक प्रबल क्षेत्र में होता है। अतः धनावेश पर आगे की ओर लगने वाला बल ऋणावेश पर पीछे की ओर लगने वाले बल से अधिक होता है, जिससे नेट बल बढ़ते हुए क्षेत्र (प्रवणता) की दिशा में लगता है, विपरीत नहीं। अतः कथन II गलत है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
कथन I और कथन II दोनों गलत हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRICCHARGESANDFIELDS_STATEMENT_Q07 - Axial and equatorial dipole field ratios and distance dependence

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: At large distances \(r \gg a\), the electric field intensity at an axial point of a short dipole is exactly twice the electric field intensity at an equatorial point at the same distance.

Statement II: The electric field intensity produced by a short electric dipole falls off with distance as \(1/r^2\), identical to the inverse-square distance dependence of an isolated point charge.

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: बड़ी दूरी \(r \gg a\) पर, एक छोटे द्विध्रुव के अक्षीय बिंदु पर विद्युत क्षेत्र की तीव्रता, समान दूरी पर स्थित निरक्षीय (विषुवतीय) बिंदु पर विद्युत क्षेत्र की तीव्रता की ठीक दोगुनी होती है।

कथन II: एक छोटे विद्युत द्विध्रुव द्वारा उत्पन्न विद्युत क्षेत्र की तीव्रता दूरी के साथ \(1/r^2\) के रूप में घटती है, जो एक एकल बिंदु आवेश के व्युत्क्रम-वर्ग दूरी निर्भरता के समान है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
For a short electric dipole of moment \(p = 2qa\), the electric field at large distances (\(r \gg a\)) is derived from vector superposition.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
At a point on the dipole axis at distance \(r\), the field magnitude is \(E_{\text{axis}} = \frac{2p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}\). At an equatorial point at the same distance \(r\), the magnitude is \(E_{\text{eq}} = \frac{p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}\). Taking their ratio gives \(\frac{E_{\text{axis}}}{E_{\text{eq}}} = 2\). Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
Because the net charge of the dipole is zero, the opposite fields of the positive and negative charges undergo destructive interference at large distances. This cancellation causes the dipole field to decay as \(1/r^3\), which is significantly faster than the \(1/r^2\) fall-off of an isolated monopolar point charge. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion:
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत:
एक छोटे विद्युत द्विध्रुव (आघूर्ण \(p = 2qa\)) के लिए बड़ी दूरी (\(r \gg a\)) पर विद्युत क्षेत्र सदिश अध्यारोपण द्वारा प्राप्त किया जाता है।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
अक्षीय स्थिति में विद्युत क्षेत्र का परिमाण \(E_{\text{axis}} = \frac{2p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}\) होता है तथा निरक्षीय स्थिति में \(E_{\text{eq}} = \frac{p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}\) होता है। अतः समान दूरी के लिए \(E_{\text{axis}} = 2 E_{\text{eq}}\) होता है। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
द्विध्रुव का कुल आवेश शून्य होने के कारण दोनों आवेशों के क्षेत्र बड़ी दूरी पर लगभग निरस्त हो जाते हैं। इसके फलस्वरूप द्विध्रुव का क्षेत्र दूरी के साथ \(1/r^3\) के रूप में घटता है, न कि एकल आवेश की भाँति \(1/r^2\) के रूप में। अतः कथन II गलत है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
कथन I सही है परंतु कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRICCHARGESANDFIELDS_STATEMENT_Q08 - Electric field inside charged spherical shell and outside infinite plane sheet

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: At any point inside a uniformly charged thin spherical shell, the electric field is non-zero and points radially away from the center of the shell.

Statement II: The electric field intensity produced by an infinitely large, uniformly charged thin plane sheet is uniform and independent of the perpendicular distance from the sheet.

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एकसमान रूप से आवेशित पतले गोलीय खोल (शेल) के भीतर किसी भी बिंदु पर विद्युत क्षेत्र अशून्य होता है और खोल के केंद्र से त्रिज्यीय रूप से बाहर की ओर दिष्ट होता है।

कथन II: एकसमान रूप से आवेशित अनंत बड़ी पतली समतल चादर द्वारा उत्पन्न विद्युत क्षेत्र की तीव्रता एकसमान होती है तथा चादर से लंबवत दूरी पर निर्भर नहीं करती है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
Gauss's law \(\oint \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{A} = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}\) determines the fields of highly symmetric charge configurations.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
For any concentric spherical Gaussian surface drawn inside a uniformly charged spherical shell (radius \(r < R\)), the enclosed charge is identically zero (\(q_{\text{enclosed}} = 0\)). Due to spherical symmetry, this strictly requires \(E = 0\) at every interior point. The field is zero everywhere inside, not non-zero. Therefore, Statement I is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
Applying Gauss's law with a cylindrical Gaussian pillbox of cross-sectional area \(A\) intersecting an infinite plane sheet of charge density \(\sigma\) yields \(2EA = \frac{\sigma A}{\varepsilon_0} \implies E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\). This expression contains no distance coordinate, proving that the field is uniform throughout space on either side. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion:
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत:
गाउस का नियम \(\oint \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{A} = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}\) सममित आवेश विन्यासों के विद्युत क्षेत्र की गणना के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
एकसमान आवेशित पतले गोलीय खोल के भीतर (\(r < R\)) खींचे गए किसी भी गाउसीय पृष्ठ के अंदर परिबद्ध आवेश शून्य होता है। गोलीय सममिति के कारण खोल के भीतर प्रत्येक बिंदु पर विद्युत क्षेत्र पूर्णतः शून्य (\(E = 0\)) होता है। अतः कथन I गलत है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
अनंत समतल चादर के लिए गाउस के नियम से फ्लक्स \(2EA = \frac{\sigma A}{\varepsilon_0}\) प्राप्त होता है, जिससे \(E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\) मिलता है। यह मान दूरी से स्वतंत्र है और पूरे अंतरिक्ष में एकसमान रहता है। अतः कथन II सही है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
कथन I गलत है परंतु कथन II सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRICCHARGESANDFIELDS_STATEMENT_Q01 - Basic properties and conservation of electric charge

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Electric charge is an intrinsic scalar property of matter and adds algebraically with proper signs.

Statement II: The total electric charge of an isolated system is conserved in any physical or chemical process.

Statement III: When a glass rod is rubbed with silk, positive charge is created on the rod by generating new protons.

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: विद्युत आवेश पदार्थ का एक आंतरिक अदिश गुण है और उचित चिन्हों के साथ इसका बीजीय योग होता है।

कथन II: किसी विलगित निकाय का कुल विद्युत आवेश किसी भी भौतिक या रासायनिक प्रक्रिया में संरक्षित रहता है।

कथन III: जब कांच की छड़ को रेशम से रगड़ा जाता है, तो नए प्रोटॉनों का निर्माण करके छड़ पर धनात्मक आवेश उत्पन्न होता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
Electric charge is a scalar physical quantity. The principle of superposition of charges states that the total charge of a system is the algebraic sum of all individual charges: \(q_{\text{net}} = \sum_{i} q_i\). Furthermore, the law of conservation of electric charge establishes that the total net charge of an isolated system remains constant over time.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
Charge has magnitude but no spatial direction; hence, it is a scalar quantity. When combining charges, positive and negative values combine algebraically (for example, \(+3\,\mu\text{C} - 5\,\mu\text{C} = -2\,\mu\text{C}\)). Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
According to the law of conservation of charge, charges can neither be created nor destroyed in isolation; they can only be transferred between interacting bodies. For any completely isolated system, the net charge is invariant under all transformations. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III:
When a glass rod is rubbed with a silk cloth, frictional work causes electrons to be transferred from the glass to the silk due to the lower work function of glass. The glass rod acquires a positive charge due to a deficiency of electrons, not because new protons are created. Protons remain tightly bound inside atomic nuclei. Therefore, Statement III is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion:
Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत:
विद्युत आवेश एक अदिश भौतिक राशि है। आवेशों के योज्यता सिद्धांत के अनुसार, किसी निकाय का कुल आवेश सभी अलग-अलग आवेशों का बीजीय योग होता है: \(q_{\text{net}} = \sum_{i} q_i\)। इसके अतिरिक्त, विद्युत आवेश संरक्षण का नियम यह स्थापित करता है कि किसी विलगित निकाय का कुल नेट आवेश समय के साथ नियत रहता है।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
आवेश में केवल परिमाण होता है और कोई स्थानिक दिशा नहीं होती; अतः यह एक अदिश राशि है। आवेशों को संयोजित करते समय, धनात्मक और ऋणात्मक मान बीजीय रूप से जुड़ते हैं (उदाहरण के लिए, \(+3\,\mu\text{C} - 5\,\mu\text{C} = -2\,\mu\text{C}\))। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
आवेश संरक्षण के नियम के अनुसार, विलगित रूप में आवेश न तो उत्पन्न किए जा सकते हैं और न ही नष्ट किए जा सकते हैं; वे केवल परस्पर क्रिया करने वाले निकायों के बीच स्थानांतरित हो सकते हैं। किसी भी पूर्णतः विलगित निकाय के लिए, कुल आवेश सभी प्रक्रियाओं में अपरिवर्तित रहता है। अतः कथन II सही है।

चरण 4: कथन III का मूल्यांकन:
जब कांच की छड़ को रेशम के कपड़े से रगड़ा जाता है, तो घर्षण कार्य के कारण कांच के कम कार्यफलन के कारण इलेक्ट्रॉन कांच से रेशम में स्थानांतरित हो जाते हैं। कांच की छड़ इलेक्ट्रॉनों की कमी के कारण धनावेशित हो जाती है, न कि नए प्रोटॉनों के निर्माण के कारण। प्रोटॉन परमाणु के नाभिक में दृढ़ता से बंधे रहते हैं। अतः कथन III गलत है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
कथन I और कथन II सही हैं, लेकिन कथन III गलत है।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statement I and Statement III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement II and Statement III are correct, but Statement I is incorrect.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRICCHARGESANDFIELDS_STATEMENT_Q02 - Properties of electrostatic field lines

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Electrostatic field lines start from positive charges and terminate at negative charges, or extend to infinity.

Statement II: Two electrostatic field lines can intersect each other at points where the electric field intensity is extremely high.

Statement III: Electrostatic field lines cannot form closed loops in an electrostatic field.

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: स्थिर-विद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाएं धनावेशों से प्रारंभ होती हैं और ऋणावेशों पर समाप्त होती हैं, या अनंत तक विस्तृत होती हैं।

कथन II: दो स्थिर-विद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाएं उन बिंदुओं पर एक-दूसरे को प्रतिच्छेद कर सकती हैं जहां विद्युत क्षेत्र की तीव्रता अत्यधिक उच्च होती है।

कथन III: स्थिर-विद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाएं स्थिर-विद्युत क्षेत्र में बंद लूप नहीं बना सकती हैं।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
An electric field line is an imaginary continuous curve drawn such that the tangent at any point gives the direction of the resultant electric field vector \(\vec{E}\) at that point. The electrostatic field is a conservative vector field derived from an electrostatic potential: \(\vec{E} = -\vec{\nabla} V\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
Electric field lines originate on positive charges (sources of field flux where \(\vec{\nabla} \cdot \vec{E} > 0\)) and terminate on negative charges (sinks of field flux where \(\vec{\nabla} \cdot \vec{E} < 0\)). For a single isolated charge, the lines diverge to or converge from infinity. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
If two field lines were to intersect at a point, two distinct tangents could be drawn at that single geometric point, implying two different directions for the resultant electric field at that same location. Because a physical vector field must have a unique, well-defined direction at every point in space, field lines can never cross or intersect under any conditions, regardless of field intensity. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III:
Because the electrostatic field is strictly conservative, the line integral of \(\vec{E}\) around any closed path is identically zero: \(\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{l} = 0\). If a field line formed a closed loop, the line integral of \(\vec{E}\) along that continuous loop would be strictly non-zero, violating the conservative nature of electrostatics. Therefore, electrostatic field lines cannot form closed loops, and Statement III is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion:
Statement I and Statement III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत:
विद्युत क्षेत्र रेखा एक काल्पनिक सतत वक्र होती है जिसे इस प्रकार खींचा जाता है कि किसी भी बिंदु पर स्पर्श रेखा उस बिंदु पर परिणामी विद्युत क्षेत्र सदिश \(\vec{E}\) की दिशा दर्शाती है। स्थिर-विद्युत क्षेत्र एक संरक्षी सदिश क्षेत्र है जिसे स्थिर-विद्युत विभव से प्राप्त किया जाता है: \(\vec{E} = -\vec{\nabla} V\)।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
विद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाएं धनावेशों से निकलती हैं (क्षेत्र फ्लक्स के स्रोत जहां \(\vec{\nabla} \cdot \vec{E} > 0\)) और ऋणावेशों पर समाप्त होती हैं (क्षेत्र फ्लक्स के सिंक जहां \(\vec{\nabla} \cdot \vec{E} < 0\))। किसी एकल विलगित आवेश के लिए, रेखाएं अनंत तक विस्तृत होती हैं या अनंत से आती हैं। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
यदि दो क्षेत्र रेखाएं किसी बिंदु पर एक-दूसरे को प्रतिच्छेद करती हैं, तो उस एकल ज्यामितीय बिंदु पर दो भिन्न स्पर्श रेखाएं खींची जा सकती हैं, जिसका अर्थ होगा कि उसी बिंदु पर परिणामी विद्युत क्षेत्र की दो भिन्न दिशाएं हैं। चूंकि एक भौतिक सदिश क्षेत्र की अंतरिक्ष के प्रत्येक बिंदु पर एक अद्वितीय, सुस्पष्ट दिशा होनी चाहिए, अतः क्षेत्र रेखाएं क्षेत्र की तीव्रता चाहे जितनी भी हो, कभी भी एक-दूसरे को प्रतिच्छेद नहीं कर सकती हैं। अतः कथन II गलत है।

चरण 4: कथन III का मूल्यांकन:
चूंकि स्थिर-विद्युत क्षेत्र पूर्णतः संरक्षी होता है, किसी भी बंद परिपथ के अनुदिश \(\vec{E}\) का रेखा समाकल सर्वसम रूप से शून्य होता है: \(\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{l} = 0\)। यदि कोई क्षेत्र रेखा बंद लूप बनाती है, तो उस सतत लूप के अनुदिश \(\vec{E}\) का रेखा समाकल अशून्य होगा, जो स्थिर-वैद्युतिकी की संरक्षी प्रकृति का उल्लंघन करेगा। अतः स्थिर-विद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाएं बंद लूप नहीं बना सकती हैं, और कथन III सही है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
कथन I और कथन III सही हैं, लेकिन कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statement I and Statement III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement II and Statement III are correct, but Statement I is incorrect.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRICCHARGESANDFIELDS_STATEMENT_Q03 - Behavior of electric dipole in uniform and non-uniform fields

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: An electric dipole placed in a uniform electric field experiences zero net translational force regardless of its orientation.

Statement II: The torque acting on an electric dipole in a uniform electric field is maximum when the dipole moment is aligned parallel to the field.

Statement III: In a non-uniform electric field, an electric dipole in general experiences both a net translational force and a torque.

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एकसमान विद्युत क्षेत्र में रखा गया एक विद्युत द्विध्रुव अपने किसी भी अभिविन्यास के लिए शून्य कुल स्थानांतरीय बल का अनुभव करता है।

कथन II: एकसमान विद्युत क्षेत्र में विद्युत द्विध्रुव पर लगने वाला बल आघूर्ण अधिकतम होता है जब द्विध्रुव आघूर्ण क्षेत्र के समांतर संरेखित होता है।

कथन III: एक असमान विद्युत क्षेत्र में, एक विद्युत द्विध्रुव सामान्यतः कुल स्थानांतरीय बल और बल आघूर्ण दोनों का अनुभव करता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
An electric dipole consists of a pair of equal and opposite point charges, \(+q\) and \(-q\), separated by a distance \(2a\), with electric dipole moment \(\vec{p} = q(2\vec{a})\). The forces on the charges are \(\vec{F}_+ = q\vec{E}_+\) and \(\vec{F}_- = -q\vec{E}_-\), giving net force \(\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = \vec{F}_+ + \vec{F}_-\) and torque \(\vec{\tau} = \vec{p} \times \vec{E}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
In a uniform electric field, \(\vec{E}\) is identical in magnitude and direction everywhere in space, so \(\vec{E}_+ = \vec{E}_- = \vec{E}\). The net force on the dipole is \(\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = q\vec{E} + (-q\vec{E}) = \vec{0}\). Because this holds true for any angle of the dipole with the field, the net translational force is identically zero in every orientation. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
The magnitude of the torque on the dipole is given by \(\tau = |\vec{p} \times \vec{E}| = p E \sin\theta\), where \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\vec{p}\) and \(\vec{E}\). When the dipole is parallel to the electric field (\(\theta = 0^\circ\)), \(\sin 0^\circ = 0\), and the torque is zero (a state of stable equilibrium). The torque is maximum when \(\theta = 90^\circ\) (perpendicular orientation), where \(\sin 90^\circ = 1\) and \(\tau_{\max} = pE\). Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III:
In a non-uniform electric field, the electric field intensities at the locations of \(+q\) and \(-q\) are unequal (\(\vec{E}_+ \neq \vec{E}_-\)). Consequently, \(\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = q(\vec{E}_+ - \vec{E}_-) \neq \vec{0}\). Additionally, since the lines of action of these unequal forces generally do not coincide, a net torque \(\vec{\tau}\) also acts on the dipole. Thus, the dipole undergoes both translational and rotational acceleration. Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion:
Statement I and Statement III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत:
एक विद्युत द्विध्रुव में \(2a\) दूरी द्वारा पृथक समान और विपरीत बिंदु आवेशों, \(+q\) और \(-q\) का एक युग्म होता है, जिसका विद्युत द्विध्रुव आघूर्ण \(\vec{p} = q(2\vec{a})\) होता है। आवेशों पर लगने वाले बल \(\vec{F}_+ = q\vec{E}_+\) और \(\vec{F}_- = -q\vec{E}_-\) होते हैं, जिससे कुल बल \(\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = \vec{F}_+ + \vec{F}_-\) और बल आघूर्ण \(\vec{\tau} = \vec{p} \times \vec{E}\) प्राप्त होता है।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
एकसमान विद्युत क्षेत्र में, \(\vec{E}\) अंतरिक्ष में सर्वत्र परिमाण और दिशा में एक समान होता है, इसलिए \(\vec{E}_+ = \vec{E}_- = \vec{E}\)। द्विध्रुव पर कुल बल \(\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = q\vec{E} + (-q\vec{E}) = \vec{0}\) होता है। चूंकि यह क्षेत्र के साथ द्विध्रुव के किसी भी कोण के लिए सत्य है, अतः प्रत्येक अभिविन्यास में कुल स्थानांतरीय बल सर्वसम रूप से शून्य होता है। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
द्विध्रुव पर बल आघूर्ण का परिमाण \(\tau = |\vec{p} \times \vec{E}| = p E \sin\theta\) द्वारा दिया जाता है, जहां \(\theta\), \(\vec{p}\) और \(\vec{E}\) के बीच का कोण है। जब द्विध्रुव विद्युत क्षेत्र के समांतर होता है (\(\theta = 0^\circ\)), तब \(\sin 0^\circ = 0\) होता है, और बल आघूर्ण शून्य होता है (स्थायी साम्यावस्था)। बल आघूर्ण अधिकतम तब होता है जब \(\theta = 90^\circ\) (लंबवत अभिविन्यास) हो, जहां \(\sin 90^\circ = 1\) और \(\tau_{\max} = pE\) होता है। अतः कथन II गलत है।

चरण 4: कथन III का मूल्यांकन:
एक असमान विद्युत क्षेत्र में, \(+q\) और \(-q\) के स्थानों पर विद्युत क्षेत्र की तीव्रताएं असमान होती हैं (\(\vec{E}_+ \neq \vec{E}_-\))। परिणामस्वरूप, \(\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = q(\vec{E}_+ - \vec{E}_-) \neq \vec{0}\)। इसके अतिरिक्त, चूंकि इन असमान बलों की क्रिया रेखाएं सामान्यतः संपाती नहीं होती हैं, अतः द्विध्रुव पर एक परिणामी बल आघूर्ण \(\vec{\tau}\) भी कार्य करता है। इस प्रकार, द्विध्रुव स्थानांतरीय और घूर्णी दोनों त्वरण का अनुभव करता है। अतः कथन III सही है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
कथन I और कथन III सही हैं, लेकिन कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRICCHARGESANDFIELDS_STATEMENT_Q04 - Gauss law applications for symmetric charge distributions

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The electrostatic field at all interior points of a uniformly charged thin spherical shell is identically zero.

Statement II: The electric field due to an infinitely long straight wire of uniform linear charge density decreases inversely with the square of distance.

Statement III: The electric field produced by an infinitely large, uniformly charged thin plane sheet is uniform and independent of distance from the sheet.

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एकसमान रूप से आवेशित पतले गोलीय खोल के सभी आंतरिक बिंदुओं पर स्थिर-विद्युत क्षेत्र सर्वसम रूप से शून्य होता है।

कथन II: एकसमान रैखिक आवेश घनत्व वाले अनंत लंबे सीधे तार के कारण विद्युत क्षेत्र दूरी के वर्ग के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती घटता है।

कथन III: एक अनंत रूप से बड़ी, एकसमान आवेशित पतली समतल चादर द्वारा उत्पन्न विद्युत क्षेत्र एकसमान होता है और चादर से दूरी पर निर्भर नहीं करता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
Gauss's law states that the total electric flux through any closed Gaussian surface equals the net charge enclosed divided by the permittivity of free space: \(\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{A} = \frac{q_{\text{enc}}}{\varepsilon_0}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
For a uniformly charged spherical shell of radius \(R\) carrying total charge \(q\), consider a concentric spherical Gaussian surface of radius \(r < R\). Because all charge resides on the surface of the shell, the enclosed charge is zero: \(q_{\text{enc}} = 0\). By spherical symmetry, \(E(4\pi r^2) = 0\), which gives \(E = 0\) at all points inside the shell. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
For an infinitely long straight wire with uniform linear charge density \(\lambda\), choose a coaxial cylindrical Gaussian surface of radius \(r\) and length \(L\). The flux through the flat circular ends is zero because \(\vec{E}\) is perpendicular to the area vectors of the ends. The curved surface area is \(2\pi r L\), and the enclosed charge is \(q_{\text{enc}} = \lambda L\). Applying Gauss's law gives \(E(2\pi r L) = \frac{\lambda L}{\varepsilon_0} \implies E = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi \varepsilon_0 r}\). Thus, the field varies inversely with distance as \(E \propto \frac{1}{r}\), not as \(1/r^2\). Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III:
For an infinite thin plane sheet with uniform surface charge density \(\sigma\), consider a cylindrical Gaussian pillbox of cross-sectional area \(A\) penetrating symmetrically through the sheet. The electric flux passes perpendicularly through the two end caps, each of area \(A\), giving a total flux of \(2EA\). The enclosed charge within the pillbox is \(q_{\text{enc}} = \sigma A\). Gauss's law yields \(2EA = \frac{\sigma A}{\varepsilon_0} \implies E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\). This expression contains no distance coordinate \(r\), proving that the electric field is completely uniform and independent of distance from the sheet. Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion:
Statement I and Statement III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: संकल्पनात्मक सिद्धांत:
गाउस का नियम बताता है कि किसी भी बंद गाउसीय पृष्ठ से गुजरने वाला कुल विद्युत फ्लक्स पृष्ठ द्वारा परिबद्ध कुल आवेश और निर्वात की विद्युतशीलता के अनुपात के बराबर होता है: \(\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{A} = \frac{q_{\text{enc}}}{\varepsilon_0}\)।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
कुल आवेश \(q\) धारण करने वाले \(R\) त्रिज्या के एकसमान आवेशित गोलीय खोल के लिए, \(r < R\) त्रिज्या के एक संकेंद्रीय गोलीय गाउसीय पृष्ठ पर विचार कीजिए। चूंकि समस्त आवेश खोल के बाह्य पृष्ठ पर स्थित होता है, इसलिए परिबद्ध आवेश शून्य होता है: \(q_{\text{enc}} = 0\)। गोलीय सममिति के कारण, \(E(4\pi r^2) = 0\), जिससे खोल के अंदर सभी बिंदुओं पर \(E = 0\) प्राप्त होता है। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
एकसमान रैखिक आवेश घनत्व \(\lambda\) वाले एक अनंत लंबे सीधे तार के लिए, \(r\) त्रिज्या और \(L\) लंबाई के एक समाक्षीय बेलनाकार गाउसीय पृष्ठ का चयन कीजिए। समतल वृत्ताकार सिरों से गुजरने वाला फ्लक्स शून्य होता है क्योंकि \(\vec{E}\) सिरों के क्षेत्रफल सदिशों के लंबवत होता है। वक्र पृष्ठ का क्षेत्रफल \(2\pi r L\) है, और परिबद्ध आवेश \(q_{\text{enc}} = \lambda L\) है। गाउस का नियम लागू करने पर \(E(2\pi r L) = \frac{\lambda L}{\varepsilon_0} \implies E = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi \varepsilon_0 r}\) प्राप्त होता है। इस प्रकार, विद्युत क्षेत्र दूरी के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती \(E \propto \frac{1}{r}\) परिवर्तित होता है, न कि \(1/r^2\) के अनुसार। अतः कथन II गलत है।

चरण 4: कथन III का मूल्यांकन:
एकसमान पृष्ठ आवेश घनत्व \(\sigma\) वाली एक अनंत पतली समतल चादर के लिए, चादर के आर-पार सममित रूप से स्थित \(A\) अनुप्रस्थ-काट क्षेत्रफल वाले एक बेलनाकार गाउसीय पिलबॉक्स पर विचार कीजिए। विद्युत फ्लक्स दोनों सिरों के अनुप्रस्थ फलकों (प्रत्येक का क्षेत्रफल \(A\)) से लंबवत बाहर निकलता है, जिससे कुल फ्लक्स \(2EA\) प्राप्त होता है। पिलबॉक्स के भीतर परिबद्ध आवेश \(q_{\text{enc}} = \sigma A\) है। गाउस का नियम देता है: \(2EA = \frac{\sigma A}{\varepsilon_0} \implies E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\)। इस व्यंजक में कोई दूरी निर्देशांक \(r\) नहीं है, जिससे सिद्ध होता है कि विद्युत क्षेत्र पूर्णतः एकसमान है और चादर से दूरी पर निर्भर नहीं करता है। अतः कथन III सही है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष:
कथन I और कथन III सही हैं, लेकिन कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement III is incorrect.
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are all correct.
Statement II and Statement III are correct, but Statement I is incorrect.
Statement I and Statement III are correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_MATCH_Q01 - SI units of fundamental electrostatic quantities

questiontext.text:
Match the physical quantities or systems in List-I with their corresponding descriptions, values, or expressions in List-II:

List-I List-II
(A) Electric charge (I) \(\text{N}\cdot\text{C}^{-1}\) or \(\text{V}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}\)
(B) Electric field (II) \(\text{C}\)
(C) Electric flux (III) \(\text{C}\cdot\text{m}\)
(D) Electric dipole moment (IV) \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{C}^{-1}\) or \(\text{V}\cdot\text{m}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
To establish the correct matching between List-I and List-II, we evaluate the scientific definition, formula, or law governing each item in List-I individually.

Step 2: Analysis of Electric charge
For Electric charge, it is measured in coulombs (\(\text{C}\)) in the SI system.

Step 3: Analysis of Electric field
For Electric field, it is defined as force per unit charge (\(\text{N}\cdot\text{C}^{-1}\)) or electric potential gradient (\(\text{V}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}\)).

Step 4: Analysis of Electric flux
For Electric flux, it is defined by the surface integral of the electric field, giving units of \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{C}^{-1}\) or \(\text{V}\cdot\text{m}\).

Step 5: Analysis of Electric dipole moment
For Electric dipole moment, it is the product of charge and separation vector, giving units of \(\text{C}\cdot\text{m}\).

Step 6: Matching Conclusion
Combining all the individual pairings yields the set of relations: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_MATCH_Q02 - Dimensional formulas of electrostatic physical quantities

questiontext.text:
Match the physical quantities or systems in List-I with their corresponding descriptions, values, or expressions in List-II:

List-I List-II
(A) Electric charge (I) \([\text{M}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-1}]\)
(B) Electric field (II) \([\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^{-3}\text{T}^4\text{A}^2]\)
(C) Electric flux (III) \([\text{T}\text{A}]\)
(D) Permittivity of free space (\(\varepsilon_0\)) (IV) \([\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-1}]\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
To establish the correct matching between List-I and List-II, we evaluate the scientific definition, formula, or law governing each item in List-I individually.

Step 2: Analysis of Electric charge
For Electric charge, it is given by current times time, \(q = I t\), yielding the dimensional formula \([\text{T}\text{A}]\).

Step 3: Analysis of Electric field
For Electric field, it is given by \(F/q = [\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-2}]/[\text{T}\text{A}] = [\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-1}]\).

Step 4: Analysis of Electric flux
For Electric flux, it is given by \(E \times \text{Area} = [\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-1}][\text{L}^2] = [\text{M}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-1}]\).

Step 5: Analysis of Permittivity of free space (\(\varepsilon_0\))
For Permittivity of free space (\(\varepsilon_0\)), it is from Coulomb's law \(\varepsilon_0 = \frac{q^2}{4\pi F r^2} = \frac{[\text{T}\text{A}]^2}{[\text{M}\text{L}\text{T}^{-2}][\text{L}^2]} = [\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^{-3}\text{T}^4\text{A}^2]\).

Step 6: Matching Conclusion
Combining all the individual pairings yields the set of relations: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

Final Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_MATCH_Q03 - Distance dependence of electrostatic field configurations

questiontext.text:
Match the physical quantities or systems in List-I with their corresponding descriptions, values, or expressions in List-II:

List-I List-II
(A) Point electric charge (I) Independent of distance \(r\)
(B) Short electric dipole (II) \(E \propto \frac{1}{r}\)
(C) Infinitely long straight charged wire (III) \(E \propto \frac{1}{r^3}\)
(D) Infinite uniformly charged thin plane sheet (IV) \(E \propto \frac{1}{r^2}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
To establish the correct matching between List-I and List-II, we evaluate the scientific definition, formula, or law governing each item in List-I individually.

Step 2: Analysis of Point electric charge
For Point electric charge, it is the electric field follows the inverse square law \(E = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q}{r^2}\), so \(E \propto \frac{1}{r^2}\).

Step 3: Analysis of Short electric dipole
For Short electric dipole, it is at distances much greater than the dipole size (\(r \gg 2a\)), the fields of the two charges largely cancel, resulting in \(E \propto \frac{1}{r^3}\).

Step 4: Analysis of Infinitely long straight charged wire
For Infinitely long straight charged wire, it is Gauss's law gives \(E = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 r}\), which shows that \(E \propto \frac{1}{r}\).

Step 5: Analysis of Infinite uniformly charged thin plane sheet
For Infinite uniformly charged thin plane sheet, it is Gauss's law gives \(E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\), which is uniform and independent of distance \(r\).

Step 6: Matching Conclusion
Combining all the individual pairings yields the set of relations: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I.

Final Answer: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_MATCH_Q04 - Electrostatic systems and corresponding governing expressions

questiontext.text:
Match the physical quantities or systems in List-I with their corresponding descriptions, values, or expressions in List-II:

List-I List-II
(A) Torque on dipole in uniform electric field (I) \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q}{r^2}\)
(B) Field on axis of short dipole at distance \(r\) (II) \(\mathbf{p} \times \mathbf{E}\)
(C) Field inside thin spherical shell of radius \(R\) (\(r < R\)) (III) Zero
(D) Field outside thin spherical shell of total charge \(q\) (\(r \ge R\)) (IV) \(\frac{2\mathbf{p}}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
To establish the correct matching between List-I and List-II, we evaluate the scientific definition, formula, or law governing each item in List-I individually.

Step 2: Analysis of Torque on dipole in uniform electric field
For Torque on dipole in uniform electric field, it is the couple formed by equal and opposite forces produces torque \(\boldsymbol{\tau} = \mathbf{p} \times \mathbf{E}\).

Step 3: Analysis of Field on axis of short dipole at distance \(r\)
For Field on axis of short dipole at distance \(r\), it is given by \(\mathbf{E} = \frac{2\mathbf{p}}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}\) pointing along the direction of the dipole moment vector.

Step 4: Analysis of Field inside thin spherical shell of radius \(R\) (\(r < R\))
For Field inside thin spherical shell of radius \(R\) (\(r < R\)), it is the Gaussian surface inside the shell encloses zero net charge, hence \(E = 0\).

Step 5: Analysis of Field outside thin spherical shell of total charge \(q\) (\(r \ge R\))
For Field outside thin spherical shell of total charge \(q\) (\(r \ge R\)), it is by Gauss's law the external field behaves as if the entire charge were at the center: \(E = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q}{r^2}\).

Step 6: Matching Conclusion
Combining all the individual pairings yields the set of relations: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I.

Final Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q01 - Number of electrons transferred during electrification

questiontext.text: A glass rod rubbed with silk acquires a positive electric charge of \(3.2 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}\). If the magnitude of elementary charge is \(e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\), find the number of electrons transferred from the glass rod to silk in units of \(10^{12}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given positive charge acquired by the glass rod: \(q = 3.2 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}\). Magnitude of elementary charge: \(e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Electrification by rubbing occurs via transfer of electrons. Acquisition of positive charge indicates a deficit of electrons equal to the charge divided by the elementary charge.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
According to the quantization of electric charge: \[q = n e \implies n = \frac{q}{e}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values into the formula: \[n = \frac{3.2 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}} = 2.0 \times 10^{12}\] The number of electrons transferred expressed in units of \(10^{12}\) is \(2.0\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The calculated electron count is an integer multiple of elementary charge and physically realistic. Hence, the value is verified.
Final Answer: 2

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q02 - Electric dipole moment of charge pair

questiontext.text: An electric dipole consists of two point charges of magnitude \(q = 2.0\,\mu\text{C}\) and \(-2.0\,\mu\text{C}\) separated by a distance of \(3.0\text{ cm}\). Calculate the magnitude of the electric dipole moment in units of \(10^{-8}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given charge magnitude: \(q = 2.0\,\mu\text{C} = 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}\). Separation between the charges: \(2a = 3.0\text{ cm} = 0.03\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
An electric dipole is defined as a pair of equal and opposite charges separated by a finite distance \(2a\). The dipole vector points from the negative charge to the positive charge.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnitude of the electric dipole moment is given by: \[p = q(2a)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values: \[p = (2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}) \times (0.03\text{ m}) = 6.0 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}\] Expressed in units of \(10^{-8}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}\), the numerical value is \(6.0\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units evaluate to Coulomb-meters, which matches the SI definition. The calculation is consistent.
Final Answer: 6

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q03 - Electric flux through inclined flat surface

questiontext.text: A uniform electric field of magnitude \(E = 500\text{ N/C}\) passes through a flat square surface of side length \(0.2\text{ m}\). The normal to the surface makes an angle of \(60^\circ\) with the direction of the electric field. Calculate the electric flux through the square surface in \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given electric field magnitude: \(E = 500\text{ N/C}\). Side length of square: \(s = 0.2\text{ m}\). Angle between the area vector (normal) and the electric field: \(\theta = 60^\circ\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The surface is flat and the field is uniform, so the dot product definition of electric flux directly applies.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Electric flux is defined by: \[\Phi = \vec{E} \cdot \vec{A} = E A \cos\theta\] where area \(A = s^2\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the area: \[A = (0.2\text{ m})^2 = 0.04\text{ m}^2\] Substitute values into the flux formula: \[\Phi = (500\text{ N/C}) \times (0.04\text{ m}^2) \times \cos 60^\circ = 500 \times 0.04 \times 0.5 = 10\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \(\text{N/C} \times \text{m}^2 = \text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}\). The value \(10\) is mathematically exact.
Final Answer: 10

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q04 - Net electric charge of four particles

questiontext.text: A system contains four point charges: \(q_1 = +3\,\mu\text{C}\), \(q_2 = -5\,\mu\text{C}\), \(q_3 = +8\,\mu\text{C}\), and \(q_4 = -2\,\mu\text{C}\). What is the total electric charge of the system in \(\mu\text{C}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given charges: \(q_1 = +3\,\mu\text{C}\), \(q_2 = -5\,\mu\text{C}\), \(q_3 = +8\,\mu\text{C}\), and \(q_4 = -2\,\mu\text{C}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Electric charge is a scalar quantity and obeys the principle of algebraic additivity for discrete point charges.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The total charge is the algebraic sum of the individual charges: \[Q = \sum_{i=1}^n q_i = q_1 + q_2 + q_3 + q_4\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Add the charges algebraically with their signs: \[Q = (+3) + (-5) + (+8) + (-2) = (3 - 5 + 8 - 2)\,\mu\text{C} = 4\,\mu\text{C}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The arithmetic sum verifies: \(11 - 7 = 4\,\mu\text{C}\).
Final Answer: 4

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q05 - Maximum torque experienced by electric dipole

questiontext.text: An electric dipole of dipole moment \(p = 4.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}\) is placed in a uniform electric field of magnitude \(E = 5.0 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}\). Calculate the maximum torque experienced by the dipole in units of \(10^{-4}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given dipole moment: \(p = 4.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}\). Electric field magnitude: \(E = 5.0 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Torque on an electric dipole depends on the angle \(\theta\) between \(\vec{p}\) and \(\vec{E}\). Maximum torque occurs when \(\vec{p}\) is perpendicular to \(\vec{E}\) (\(\sin\theta = 1\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnitude of torque is: \[\tau = p E \sin\theta \implies \tau_{\max} = p E\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the maximum torque: \[\tau_{\max} = (4.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}) \times (5.0 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}) = 2.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}\] Expressed in units of \(10^{-4}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}\), the value is \(2.0\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \(\text{C}\cdot\text{m} \times \text{N/C} = \text{N}\cdot\text{m}\), which correctly represents torque.
Final Answer: 2

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q06 - Electric field produced by point charge

questiontext.text: Calculate the magnitude of the electric field at a distance of \(0.3\text{ m}\) from an isolated point charge of \(4.0\,\mu\text{C}\) in vacuum. Express your answer in units of \(10^5\text{ N/C}\). (Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given point charge: \(q = 4.0\,\mu\text{C} = 4.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}\). Distance: \(r = 0.3\text{ m}\). Coulomb constant: \(k = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\\text{C}^2\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The point charge is situated in vacuum. The electric field is spherically symmetric and radially directed outwards.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnitude of the electric field due to a point charge is: \[E = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{q}{r^2}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[E = \frac{(9.0 \times 10^9) \times (4.0 \times 10^{-6})}{(0.3)^2} = \frac{36.0 \times 10^3}{0.09} = 4.0 \times 10^5\text{ N/C}\] Expressed in units of \(10^5\text{ N/C}\), the numerical value is \(4.0\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking dimensions: \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2 \times \text{C} / \text{m}^2 = \text{N/C}\). The value is confirmed.
Final Answer: 4

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q07 - Total electric flux from enclosed charge

questiontext.text: A point charge of \(8.854\text{ nC}\) is positioned at the center of a closed spherical Gaussian surface in vacuum. What is the total electric flux leaving through the Gaussian surface in \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}\)? (Take \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.854 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2)\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given enclosed charge: \(q = 8.854\text{ nC} = 8.854 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}\). Permittivity of free space: \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.854 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2)\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Gauss's law states that the total outward electric flux through any closed Gaussian surface depends solely on the net charge enclosed, independent of its shape or size.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Gauss's law formula: \[\Phi = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values: \[\Phi = \frac{8.854 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}}{8.854 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2)} = 1000\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units simplify to \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}\). The arithmetic evaluates exactly to \(1000\).
Final Answer: 1000

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q08 - Coulomb force between two charged spheres

questiontext.text: Two small charged spheres carrying charges \(q_1 = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}\) and \(q_2 = 3.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}\) are placed \(30\text{ cm}\) apart in air. Calculate the magnitude of the electrostatic force between them in milliNewtons (\(\text{mN}\)). (Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given charges: \(q_1 = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}\), \(q_2 = 3.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}\). Separation: \(r = 30\text{ cm} = 0.30\text{ m}\). Coulomb constant: \(k = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The spheres are small compared to the separation distance, so they can be treated as point charges. Dielectric constant of air is taken as approximately \(1\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Coulomb's law gives the electrostatic force between two point charges: \[F = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{q_1 q_2}{r^2}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[F = \frac{(9.0 \times 10^9) \times (2.0 \times 10^{-7}) \times (3.0 \times 10^{-7})}{(0.30)^2} = \frac{5.4 \times 10^{-3}}{0.09} = 6.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ N}\] Converting to milliNewtons: \[F = 6.0\text{ mN}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both charges are positive, so the force is repulsive. The magnitude is \(6.0\text{ mN}\).
Final Answer: 6

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q09 - Separation distance from known Coulomb force

questiontext.text: Two identical point charges of \(4.0\,\mu\text{C}\) each repel each other with an electrostatic force of \(0.9\text{ N}\) in air. Find the separation distance between the two charges in meters. (Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given charges: \(q_1 = q_2 = 4.0\,\mu\text{C} = 4.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}\). Repulsive force: \(F = 0.9\text{ N}\). Coulomb constant: \(k = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The charges are treated as isolated point charges in air with relative permittivity \(\varepsilon_r = 1\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Coulomb's law formula relates force to separation distance: \[F = \frac{k q_1 q_2}{r^2} \implies r = \sqrt{\frac{k q^2}{F}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the numerical parameters: \[r^2 = \frac{(9.0 \times 10^9) \times (4.0 \times 10^{-6})^2}{0.9} = \frac{(9.0 \times 10^9) \times (16.0 \times 10^{-12})}{0.9} = \frac{0.144}{0.9} = 0.16\text{ m}^2\] Taking the square root: \[r = \sqrt{0.16} = 0.4\text{ m}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \(\sqrt{\frac{\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2 \cdot \text{C}^2}{\text{N}}} = \text{m}\). Distance must be positive, giving \(0.4\text{ m}\).
Final Answer: 0.4

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q10 - Linear charge density of infinite wire

questiontext.text: An infinitely long straight line of charge produces an electric field of magnitude \(9.0 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}\) at a radial distance of \(2.0\text{ cm}\) in free space. Calculate the linear charge density \(\lambda\) in \(\mu\text{C/m}\). (Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given electric field: \(E = 9.0 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}\). Radial distance: \(r = 2.0\text{ cm} = 0.02\text{ m}\). Constant: \(\frac{1}{2\pi\varepsilon_0} = 2k = 18.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
By applying Gauss's law with a cylindrical Gaussian surface coaxial with the line charge, end-cap fluxes are zero and cylindrical wall flux yields the field.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The electric field due to an infinite line charge is: \[E = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 r} = \frac{2k\lambda}{r} \implies \lambda = \frac{E r}{2k}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[\lambda = \frac{(9.0 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}) \times (0.02\text{ m})}{2 \times (9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2)} = \frac{1800}{1.8 \times 10^{10}} = 1.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C/m}\] Convert to \(\mu\text{C/m}\): \[\lambda = 0.1\,\mu\text{C/m}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Dimensional verification gives Coulombs per meter. The value \(0.1\,\mu\text{C/m}\) is consistent.
Final Answer: 0.1

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q11 - Electric field of infinite plane sheet

questiontext.text: An infinite thin plane sheet of charge has a uniform surface charge density \(\sigma = 1.77 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C/m}^2\). Calculate the magnitude of the electric field near the sheet in \(\text{kV/m}\). (Take \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2)\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given surface charge density: \(\sigma = 1.77 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C/m}^2\). Permittivity: \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2)\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The sheet is taken to be infinitely large and uniformly charged, so the electric field is uniform, perpendicular to the sheet, and independent of distance from the plane.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
By Gauss's law, the electric field due to an infinite thin plane sheet of charge is: \[E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given parameters: \[E = \frac{1.77 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C/m}^2}{2 \times (8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2))} = \frac{1.77 \times 10^{-7}}{1.77 \times 10^{-11}} = 10^4\text{ N/C}\] Convert to \(\text{kV/m}\): \[E = \frac{10^4}{1000}\text{ kV/m} = 10\text{ kV/m}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio \(1.77 / 1.77 = 1\) leaves \(10^4\text{ N/C} = 10\text{ kV/m}\). The solution is exact.
Final Answer: 10

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q12 - Axial electric field of small dipole

questiontext.text: An electric dipole consists of two charges \(\pm 5.0\,\mu\text{C}\) separated by a distance of \(4.0\text{ mm}\). Calculate the magnitude of the electric field at an axial point located at a distance of \(10\text{ cm}\) from the center of the dipole in units of \(10^5\text{ N/C}\). (Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given charge magnitude: \(q = 5.0\,\mu\text{C} = 5.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}\). Separation: \(2a = 4.0\text{ mm} = 4.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}\). Distance from dipole center: \(r = 10\text{ cm} = 0.10\text{ m}\). Constant: \(k = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Since \(r = 10\text{ cm} \gg a = 0.2\text{ cm}\) (specifically \(r/a = 50\)), the short dipole approximation \(r^2 \gg a^2\) is applicable with very high accuracy.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Electric dipole moment is \(p = q(2a)\). The axial electric field for a short dipole is given by: \[E_{\text{axial}} = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{2p}{r^3}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate dipole moment: \[p = (5.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}) \times (4.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}) = 2.0 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}\] Substitute into the axial field formula: \[E_{\text{axial}} = \frac{(9.0 \times 10^9) \times 2 \times (2.0 \times 10^{-8})}{(0.10)^3} = \frac{360}{0.001} = 3.6 \times 10^5\text{ N/C}\] Expressed in units of \(10^5\text{ N/C}\), the value is \(3.6\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2 \times (\text{C}\cdot\text{m})/\text{m}^3 = \text{N/C}\). The value is confirmed.
Final Answer: 3.6

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q13 - Equatorial electric field of short dipole

questiontext.text: An electric dipole has a dipole moment of \(p = 2.0 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}\). Calculate the magnitude of the electric field at an equatorial point located at a distance of \(10\text{ cm}\) from the center of the dipole in units of \(10^5\text{ N/C}\). (Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given electric dipole moment: \(p = 2.0 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}\). Equatorial distance from dipole center: \(r = 10\text{ cm} = 0.10\text{ m}\). Coulomb constant: \(k = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The observation distance \(r\) is much larger than the dipole separation, allowing the short dipole approximation.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnitude of the electric field on the equatorial plane of a short dipole is given by: \[E_{\text{eq}} = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{p}{r^3}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given parameters: \[E_{\text{eq}} = \frac{(9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2) \times (2.0 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m})}{(0.10\text{ m})^3} = \frac{180}{0.001} = 1.8 \times 10^5\text{ N/C}\] Expressed in units of \(10^5\text{ N/C}\), the numerical value is \(1.8\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Dimensional verification yields \(\text{N/C}\). Notice that at identical distances, \(E_{\text{axial}} = 2 E_{\text{eq}}\), which validates the calculation.
Final Answer: 1.8

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q14 - Acceleration of electron in uniform field

questiontext.text: An electron of mass \(m = 9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}\) and charge magnitude \(e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\) moves in a uniform electric field of magnitude \(E = 1.82 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}\). Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of the electron in units of \(10^{15}\text{ m/s}^2\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given electron mass: \(m = 9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}\). Elementary charge: \(e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\). Electric field: \(E = 1.82 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Gravitational force on the electron is negligible compared to the electrostatic force. Newton's second law is applied in an inertial frame.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The electrostatic force is \(F = e E\). By Newton's second law: \[a = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{e E}{m}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[a = \frac{(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}) \times (1.82 \times 10^4\text{ N/C})}{9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}} = \frac{2.912 \times 10^{-15}\text{ N}}{9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}} = 3.2 \times 10^{15}\text{ m/s}^2\] Expressed in units of \(10^{15}\text{ m/s}^2\), the value is \(3.2\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \(\text{N/kg} = (\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}^2)/\text{kg} = \text{m/s}^2\). The value is verified.
Final Answer: 3.2

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q15 - Electric flux through single cube face

questiontext.text: A point charge of \(5.31 \times 10^{-11}\text{ C}\) is placed at the exact center of a closed cubical box. Calculate the electric flux passing through any one face of the cube in \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}\). (Take \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2)\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given charge enclosed at center of cube: \(q = 5.31 \times 10^{-11}\text{ C}\). Permittivity of free space: \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2)\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
By symmetry, because the point charge is situated at the geometric center of the cube, the electric flux is symmetrically distributed and identical through each of the six faces.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
By Gauss's law, total flux is \(\Phi_{\text{total}} = \frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\). The flux through one face is: \[\Phi_{\text{face}} = \frac{\Phi_{\text{total}}}{6} = \frac{q}{6\varepsilon_0}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[\Phi_{\text{face}} = \frac{5.31 \times 10^{-11}\text{ C}}{6 \times (8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2))} = \frac{5.31 \times 10^{-11}}{5.31 \times 10^{-11}} = 1.0\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Dimensional analysis yields \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}\). The denominator \(6 \times 8.85 = 53.1\) matches the numerator, giving \(1.0\).
Final Answer: 1

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q16 - Electric field outside charged spherical shell

questiontext.text: A thin spherical conducting shell of radius \(R = 10\text{ cm}\) carries a total charge of \(2.0\,\mu\text{C}\) uniformly distributed over its surface. Calculate the magnitude of the electric field at a distance of \(30\text{ cm}\) from the center of the shell in \(\text{kV/m}\). (Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given radius of shell: \(R = 10\text{ cm} = 0.10\text{ m}\). Total charge: \(q = 2.0\,\mu\text{C} = 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}\). Distance from center: \(r = 30\text{ cm} = 0.30\text{ m}\). Constant: \(k = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Since \(r > R\), the observation point lies outside the shell. By Gauss's law, a uniformly charged spherical shell behaves for all external points as if all its charge were concentrated at its center.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The electric field at an external point is: \[E = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{q}{r^2}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[E = \frac{(9.0 \times 10^9) \times (2.0 \times 10^{-6})}{(0.30)^2} = \frac{1.8 \times 10^4}{0.09} = 2.0 \times 10^5\text{ N/C}\] Convert to \(\text{kV/m}\): \[E = \frac{2.0 \times 10^5}{10^3}\text{ kV/m} = 200\text{ kV/m}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units check: \(2.0 \times 10^5\text{ N/C} = 200\text{ kV/m}\). The arithmetic is exact.
Final Answer: 200

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q17 - Electric field inside charged spherical shell

questiontext.text: A thin spherical conducting shell of radius \(R = 10\text{ cm}\) carries a total charge of \(2.0\,\mu\text{C}\) uniformly distributed on its surface. What is the magnitude of the electric field at a distance of \(5.0\text{ cm}\) from the center of the shell in \(\text{N/C}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given radius of shell: \(R = 10\text{ cm}\). Total charge on shell surface: \(q = 2.0\,\mu\text{C}\). Radial distance of field point: \(r = 5.0\text{ cm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Since \(r < R\), the field point lies entirely inside the hollow spherical shell. Consider a concentric spherical Gaussian surface of radius \(r = 5.0\text{ cm}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
According to Gauss's law: \[\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{A} = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Because all charge resides strictly on the outer surface of the shell, the charge enclosed by the Gaussian surface of radius \(r = 5.0\text{ cm}\) is zero: \[q_{\text{enclosed}} = 0\] Therefore: \[E (4\pi r^2) = 0 \implies E = 0\text{ N/C}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Electrostatic shielding and Gauss's law both confirm that the electric field inside a uniformly charged conducting spherical shell is identically zero.
Final Answer: 0

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q18 - Mass transferred during negative charging process

questiontext.text: A polythene piece rubbed with wool is found to have a negative charge of \(3.2 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}\). Calculate the mass transferred from wool to polythene during this process in units of \(10^{-18}\text{ kg}\). (Take elementary charge \(e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\) and mass of an electron \(m_e = 9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given acquired negative charge: \(q = -3.2 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}\). Elementary charge: \(e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\). Mass of an electron: \(m_e = 9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
A negative charge signifies an excess of electrons transferred from the wool to the polythene. Each electron carries both charge \(-e\) and rest mass \(m_e\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Number of transferred electrons is \(n = \frac{|q|}{e}\). The total mass transferred is: \[\Delta m = n m_e = \left(\frac{|q|}{e}\right) m_e\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the number of electrons: \[n = \frac{3.2 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}} = 2.0 \times 10^{12}\] Calculate the total mass transferred: \[\Delta m = (2.0 \times 10^{12}) \times (9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}) = 18.2 \times 10^{-19}\text{ kg} = 1.82 \times 10^{-18}\text{ kg}\] In units of \(10^{-18}\text{ kg}\), the value is \(1.82\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The mass is positive and negligible on macroscopic scales, consistent with electrostatic rubbing phenomena.
Final Answer: 1.82

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q19 - Null point location between two charges

questiontext.text: Two positive point charges \(+q\) and \(+4q\) are fixed at a distance of \(30\text{ cm}\) apart in vacuum. At what distance (in \(\text{cm}\)) from the charge \(+q\) along the line joining the two charges is the net electric field equal to zero?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given charges: \(q_1 = +q\), \(q_2 = +4q\). Total separation distance: \(L = 30\text{ cm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Both charges are positive, so their electric fields point away from each charge. Along the line segment joining them, the two electric fields point in opposite directions and can cancel out.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Let the null point be at distance \(x\) from \(+q\) and \((L - x)\) from \(+4q\). Equating the magnitudes of the electric fields: \[\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{q}{x^2} = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{4q}{(L - x)^2}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Simplify by canceling common terms: \[\frac{1}{x^2} = \frac{4}{(L - x)^2}\] Taking the positive square root on both sides (since the point lies between the charges, \(0 < x < L\)): \[\frac{1}{x} = \frac{2}{L - x} \implies L - x = 2x \implies 3x = L\] Substitute \(L = 30\text{ cm}\): \[x = \frac{30\text{ cm}}{3} = 10\text{ cm}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The null point is closer to the smaller charge \(q\), as expected from the inverse-square law.
Final Answer: 10

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q20 - Force on charge midway between dipole

questiontext.text: Two point charges \(q_1 = +2.0\,\mu\text{C}\) and \(q_2 = -2.0\,\mu\text{C}\) are placed \(20\text{ cm}\) apart in air. Find the magnitude of the electrostatic force acting on a test charge \(q_0 = +1.0\text{ nC}\) placed midway between them, in milliNewtons (\(\text{mN}\)). (Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given charges: \(q_1 = +2.0\,\mu\text{C} = 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}\), \(q_2 = -2.0\,\mu\text{C} = -2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}\). Distance between charges: \(2d = 20\text{ cm}\), so distance from each charge to the midpoint is \(d = 10\text{ cm} = 0.10\text{ m}\). Test charge: \(q_0 = +1.0\text{ nC} = 1.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
At the midpoint, the electric field due to the positive charge points away from it (toward the negative charge). The electric field due to the negative charge points toward it (also in the same direction). Hence, the two fields add vectorially.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The net electric field at the midpoint is: \[E_{\text{net}} = E_1 + E_2 = 2 \left(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{|q|}{d^2}\right)\] The force on the test charge is \(F = q_0 E_{\text{net}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \(E_{\text{net}}\): \[E_{\text{net}} = 2 \times \frac{(9.0 \times 10^9) \times (2.0 \times 10^{-6})}{(0.10)^2} = 2 \times \frac{1.8 \times 10^4}{0.01} = 3.6 \times 10^6\text{ N/C}\] Calculate force: \[F = (1.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}) \times (3.6 \times 10^6\text{ N/C}) = 3.6 \times 10^{-3}\text{ N} = 3.6\text{ mN}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both forces push/pull in the same direction, yielding \(3.6\text{ mN}\).
Final Answer: 3.6

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q21 - Work done rotating dipole in field

questiontext.text: An electric dipole of dipole moment \(p = 2.0 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}\) is aligned parallel to a uniform electric field of magnitude \(E = 5.0 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}\). Calculate the work done by an external agent to rotate the dipole by \(180^\circ\) from its initial stable orientation, in milliJoules (\(\text{mJ}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given dipole moment: \(p = 2.0 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}\). Electric field: \(E = 5.0 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}\). Initial angle: \(\theta_1 = 0^\circ\). Final angle: \(\theta_2 = 180^\circ\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The dipole is rotated quasi-statically without change in kinetic energy against the electrostatic torque.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The work done by an external torque is equal to the increase in potential energy: \[W = \Delta U = -p E \cos\theta_2 - (-p E \cos\theta_1) = p E (\cos\theta_1 - \cos\theta_2)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[W = p E [\cos 0^\circ - \cos 180^\circ] = p E [1 - (-1)] = 2 p E\] \[W = 2 \times (2.0 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}) \times (5.0 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}) = 2.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ J}\] Convert to milliJoules: \[W = 2.0\text{ mJ}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Work done is positive because work is supplied against the aligning electrostatic torque.
Final Answer: 2

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q22 - Enclosed charge determined from electric flux

questiontext.text: A closed Gaussian surface encloses a net electric charge. The total outward electric flux measured through the entire surface is \(4.52 \times 10^5\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}\). Find the net charge enclosed inside the surface in \(\mu\text{C}\). (Take \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2)\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given total outward electric flux: \(\Phi = 4.52 \times 10^5\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}\). Permittivity of free space: \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2)\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Gauss's law applies to any closed surface regardless of its geometric shape.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
According to Gauss's law: \[\Phi = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0} \implies q_{\text{enclosed}} = \varepsilon_0 \Phi\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values: \[q_{\text{enclosed}} = (8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2)) \times (4.52 \times 10^5\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}) = 4.0002 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}\] Expressed in \(\mu\text{C}\): \[q_{\text{enclosed}} = 4.0\,\mu\text{C}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Dimensional verification: \(\text{C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2) \times \text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C} = \text{C}\). Value is \(4.0\,\mu\text{C}\).
Final Answer: 4

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q23 - Total charge on charged conducting sphere

questiontext.text: A uniformly charged conducting sphere of diameter \(2.4\text{ m}\) has a surface charge density of \(\sigma = 80.0\,\mu\text{C/m}^2\). Calculate the total electric charge on the sphere in milliCoulombs (\(\text{mC}\)). (Take \(\pi = 3.1416\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given sphere diameter: \(D = 2.4\text{ m}\), so radius \(R = 1.2\text{ m}\). Surface charge density: \(\sigma = 80.0\,\mu\text{C/m}^2 = 80.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C/m}^2\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
On a conducting sphere, excess charge resides entirely and uniformly on its outer spherical surface.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The total charge is equal to surface charge density multiplied by total surface area: \[Q = \sigma A = \sigma (4\pi R^2)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate surface area: \[A = 4\pi (1.2\text{ m})^2 = 4 \times 3.1416 \times 1.44 = 18.0956\text{ m}^2\] Calculate total charge: \[Q = (80.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C/m}^2) \times 18.0956\text{ m}^2 = 1.4476 \times 10^{-3}\text{ C} = 1.45\text{ mC}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \(\text{C/m}^2 \times \text{m}^2 = \text{C}\). Rounding to three significant figures gives \(1.45\text{ mC}\).
Final Answer: 1.45

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTRIC_CHARGES_AND_FIELDS_NUMERICAL_Q24 - Electric field between oppositely charged plates

questiontext.text: Two large, thin metal plates are placed parallel and close to each other. On their inner faces, the plates carry uniform surface charge densities of opposite signs and magnitude \(\sigma = 17.7 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C/m}^2\). Calculate the electric field in the region between the plates in \(\text{N/C}\). (Take \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2)\)).

generalfeedback.text:
