Therefore, Statement I is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
On the equatorial plane, every point is equidistant from the positive charge \(+q\) and negative charge \(-q\) of the dipole (i.e., \(r_+ = r_-\)). The total potential is the algebraic sum of the individual scalar potentials: \[ V = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \left( \frac{q}{r_+} + \frac{-q}{r_-} \right) = 0 \] Equivalently, substituting \(\theta = 90^\circ\) into the dipole potential formula gives \(\cos 90^\circ = 0\), yielding \(V = 0\) across the entire equatorial plane. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Conclusion
Statement I fails because dipole potential drops as \(1/r^2\), whereas Statement II is correct because the equatorial plane is a zero-potential plane.

Final Conceptual Answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
द्विध्रुव आघूर्ण \(\mathbf{p}\) वाले एक छोटे विद्युत द्विध्रुव के कारण \(\hat{\mathbf{r}}\) दिशा में दूरी \(r\) पर स्थिर-वैद्युत विभव का सूत्र निम्न है: \[ V(r, \theta) = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{p \cos\theta}{r^2} \] अक्षीय रेखा पर (\(\theta = 0^\circ\) या \(\theta = 180^\circ\)), विभव \(V = \pm \frac{p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}\) होता है, जो दूरी के वर्ग के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती (\(V \propto 1/r^2\)) होता है, न कि \(1/r\) (जो कि एकल बिंदु आवेश का अभिलक्षण है)। अतः, कथन I गलत है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
निरक्षीय (विषुवतीय) तल पर प्रत्येक बिंदु द्विध्रुव के धनात्मक आवेश \(+q\) और ऋणात्मक आवेश \(-q\) से समान दूरी पर स्थित होता है (अर्थात् \(r_+ = r_-\))। कुल विभव दोनों अदिश विभवों का बीजगणितीय योग होता है: \[ V = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \left( \frac{q}{r_+} + \frac{-q}{r_-} \right) = 0 \] समीकरण में \(\theta = 90^\circ\) रखने पर भी \(\cos 90^\circ = 0\) प्राप्त होता है, जिससे पूरे निरक्षीय तल पर \(V = 0\) होता है। अतः, कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: निष्कर्ष
कथन I गलत है क्योंकि द्विध्रुव विभव \(1/r^2\) के रूप में घटता है, जबकि कथन II सही है क्योंकि निरक्षीय तल एक शून्य-विभव तल होता है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: कथन I गलत है लेकिन कथन II सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH02_ST2_Q04 - Electrostatic properties inside a charged spherical conducting shell

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The electrostatic potential inside a uniformly charged thin spherical shell is zero at all interior points.

Statement II: The electric field inside a uniformly charged thin spherical shell increases linearly from zero at the center to a maximum at the surface.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एकसमान रूप से आवेशित पतले गोलीय कोश के अंदर सभी आंतरिक बिंदुओं पर स्थिर-वैद्युत विभव शून्य होता है।

कथन II: एकसमान रूप से आवेशित पतले गोलीय कोश के अंदर विद्युत क्षेत्र केंद्र पर शून्य से पृष्ठ पर अधिकतम तक रैखिक रूप से बढ़ता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
For a thin spherical shell of radius \(R\) carrying total charge \(Q\), the electric field at any interior point (\(r < R\)) is identically zero by Gauss's law (\(\oint \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{A} = q_{\text{enclosed}}/\varepsilon_0 = 0\)). Since \(\mathbf{E} = -\nabla V = 0\), the electric potential \(V\) must be constant throughout the interior volume and equal to its value on the surface: \[ V(r) = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{Q}{R} \quad \text{for } r \le R \] It is not zero (unless \(Q = 0\)). Therefore, Statement I is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
As established by Gauss's law, no charge is enclosed by a Gaussian surface of radius \(r < R\) inside the shell. Consequently, the electric field is strictly zero at every point inside the spherical shell (\(E = 0\) for all \(0 \le r < R\)). It does not increase linearly (a linear increase \(E \propto r\) occurs inside a uniformly charged non-conducting solid sphere, not a shell). Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 3: Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect regarding the interior of a charged thin spherical shell.

Final Conceptual Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
त्रिज्या \(R\) और कुल आवेश \(Q\) वाले पतले गोलीय कोश के अंदर किसी भी आंतरिक बिंदु (\(r < R\)) पर विद्युत क्षेत्र गाउस के नियम के अनुसार पूर्णतः शून्य होता है (\(\oint \mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{A} = q_{\text{enclosed}}/\varepsilon_0 = 0\))। चूँकि \(\mathbf{E} = -\nabla V = 0\), अतः पूरे आंतरिक आयतन में विद्युत विभव \(V\) नियत रहता है और पृष्ठ पर इसके मान के बराबर होता है: \[ V(r) = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{Q}{R} \quad (r \le R \text{ के लिए}) \] यह शून्य नहीं होता है (जब तक कि \(Q = 0\) न हो)। इसलिए, कथन I गलत है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
गाउस के नियम से, कोश के भीतर \(r < R\) त्रिज्या वाले गाउसीय पृष्ठ द्वारा कोई आवेश परिबद्ध नहीं होता है। फलस्वरूप, गोलीय कोश के भीतर प्रत्येक बिंदु पर विद्युत क्षेत्र पूर्णतः शून्य होता है (सभी \(0 \le r < R\) के लिए \(E = 0\))। यह रैखिक रूप से नहीं बढ़ता (रैखिक वृद्धि \(E \propto r\) एकसमान आवेशित अचालक ठोस गोले के अंदर होती है, कोश में नहीं)। इसलिए, कथन II गलत है।

चरण 3: निष्कर्ष
आवेशित पतले गोलीय कोश के आंतरिक भाग के संदर्भ में दोनों कथन गलत हैं।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: दोनों कथन I और कथन II गलत हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH02_ST2_Q05 - Independence of capacitance from charge and potential difference

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The capacitance \(C\) of a parallel-plate capacitor depends on the shape, size, and geometrical separation of the conductors as well as the medium between them.

Statement II: The capacitance \(C\) of a capacitor is independent of the charge \(Q\) residing on the plates and the potential difference \(V\) between them.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: समांतर पट्टिका संधारित्र की धारिता \(C\) चालकों की आकृति, आकार और उनके बीच की ज्यामितीय दूरी तथा उनके बीच के माध्यम पर निर्भर करती है।

कथन II: किसी संधारित्र की धारिता \(C\) पट्टिकाओं पर उपस्थित आवेश \(Q\) और उनके बीच के विभवांतर \(V\) से स्वतंत्र होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is given by \(C = \frac{\varepsilon A}{d} = \frac{\varepsilon_r \varepsilon_0 A}{d}\), where \(A\) is the plate area (size and geometry), \(d\) is the separation distance, and \(\varepsilon_r\) is the relative permittivity of the insulating dielectric medium. Thus, \(C\) depends entirely on geometric configuration and the dielectric medium. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
Although capacitance is mathematically defined as the ratio \(C = Q/V\), the potential difference \(V\) is directly proportional to the charge \(Q\) on the conductor (\(V \propto Q\)). As a result, increasing \(Q\) increases \(V\) by the exact same factor, maintaining a constant ratio \(Q/V\). Thus, capacitance is an intrinsic property of the system of conductors and is independent of \(Q\) and \(V\). Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Conclusion
Both statements correctly explain the physical dependencies and nature of electrical capacitance.

Final Conceptual Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
समांतर पट्टिका संधारित्र की धारिता का सूत्र \(C = \frac{\varepsilon A}{d} = \frac{\varepsilon_r \varepsilon_0 A}{d}\) होता है, जहाँ \(A\) पट्टिका का क्षेत्रफल (आकार और ज्यामिति), \(d\) पट्टिकाओं के बीच की दूरी तथा \(\varepsilon_r\) परावैद्युत माध्यम की आपेक्षिक विद्युतशीलता है। अतः, \(C\) पूर्ण रूप से ज्यामितीय विन्यास और परावैद्युत माध्यम पर निर्भर करता है। इसलिए, कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
यद्यपि धारिता को गणितीय रूप से अनुपात \(C = Q/V\) के रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है, परंतु चालक पर उपस्थित आवेश \(Q\) उसके विभवांतर \(V\) के समानुपाती होता है (\(V \propto Q\))। परिणामस्वरूप, \(Q\) को बढ़ाने पर \(V\) भी उसी अनुपात में बढ़ जाता है, जिससे अनुपात \(Q/V\) सदैव नियत रहता है। अतः, धारिता चालक निकाय का एक आंतरिक गुण है जो \(Q\) और \(V\) पर निर्भर नहीं करता। इसलिए, कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: निष्कर्ष
दोनों कथन विद्युत धारिता की भौतिक निर्भरता और प्रकृति की सही व्याख्या करते हैं।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: दोनों कथन I और कथन II सही हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH02_ST2_Q06 - Dielectric slab insertion in parallel plate capacitor

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When a dielectric slab of dielectric constant \(K > 1\) and thickness \(t < d\) is inserted between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor of plate separation \(d\), its capacitance increases.

Statement II: The electric field inside the dielectric slab is stronger than the original electric field in the vacuum region between the plates.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: जब पट्टिका पृथक्करण \(d\) वाले समांतर पट्टिका संधारित्र की पट्टिकाओं के बीच परावैद्युतांक \(K > 1\) और मोटाई \(t < d\) की एक परावैद्युत पट्टिका रखी जाती है, तो इसकी धारिता बढ़ जाती है।

कथन II: परावैद्युत पट्टिका के अंदर विद्युत क्षेत्र, पट्टिकाओं के बीच निर्वात क्षेत्र के मूल विद्युत क्षेत्र की तुलना में अधिक प्रबल होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
With air/vacuum, the capacitance is \(C_0 = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}\). When a dielectric slab of thickness \(t\) and dielectric constant \(K\) is introduced, the effective separation becomes: \[ d_{\text{eff}} = (d - t) + \frac{t}{K} = d - t\left(1 - \frac{1}{K}\right) \] Since \(K > 1\), the term \(1 - 1/K > 0\), which makes \(d_{\text{eff}} < d\). Consequently, the new capacitance is: \[ C = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d - t\left(1 - \frac{1}{K}\right)} > C_0 \] Thus, the capacitance increases. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
When a dielectric is placed in an external electric field \(\mathbf{E}_0\), dielectric polarization occurs, inducing bound charges on the faces of the slab. These induced surface charges produce an internal reverse electric field \(\mathbf{E}_p\). The net electric field inside the dielectric is given by: \[ E = E_0 - E_p = \frac{E_0}{K} \] Since \(K > 1\), the electric field inside the dielectric slab is strictly weaker than \(E_0\), not stronger. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 3: Conclusion
Statement I is correct because dielectric insertion always reduces effective separation and increases capacitance, while Statement II is incorrect because polarization reduces the electric field within the dielectric.

Final Conceptual Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
वायु/निर्वात की स्थिति में धारिता \(C_0 = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}\) होती है। जब मोटाई \(t\) और परावैद्युतांक \(K\) की एक परावैद्युत पट्टिका रखी जाती है, तो प्रभावी दूरी निम्न हो जाती है: \[ d_{\text{eff}} = (d - t) + \frac{t}{K} = d - t\left(1 - \frac{1}{K}\right) \] चूँकि \(K > 1\) है, अतः पद \(1 - 1/K > 0\) होता है, जिससे \(d_{\text{eff}} < d\) हो जाता है। परिणामस्वरूप, नई धारिता: \[ C = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d - t\left(1 - \frac{1}{K}\right)} > C_0 \] अतः, धारिता बढ़ जाती है। इसलिए, कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
जब किसी परावैद्युत को बाह्य विद्युत क्षेत्र \(\mathbf{E}_0\) में रखा जाता है, तो परावैद्युत ध्रुवण के कारण पट्टिका के फलकों पर प्रेरित परिबद्ध आवेश उत्पन्न होते हैं। ये प्रेरित आवेश एक आंतरिक विपरीत विद्युत क्षेत्र \(\mathbf{E}_p\) उत्पन्न करते हैं। परावैद्युत के अंदर कुल विद्युत क्षेत्र निम्न होता है: \[ E = E_0 - E_p = \frac{E_0}{K} \] चूँकि \(K > 1\) है, इसलिए परावैद्युत पट्टिका के अंदर विद्युत क्षेत्र \(E_0\) से दुर्बल (कम) होता है, न कि अधिक प्रबल। इसलिए, कथन II गलत है।

चरण 3: निष्कर्ष
कथन I सही है क्योंकि परावैद्युत रखने पर धारिता बढ़ती है, जबकि कथन II गलत है क्योंकि ध्रुवण के कारण परावैद्युत के भीतर विद्युत क्षेत्र घट जाता है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: कथन I सही है लेकिन कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH02_ST2_Q07 - Electrostatic energy variation on dielectric insertion in isolated vs battery connected capacitor

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When a dielectric slab of dielectric constant \(K > 1\) is inserted into a capacitor connected across a battery of constant voltage \(V\), the electrostatic energy stored in the capacitor decreases.

Statement II: When a dielectric slab of dielectric constant \(K > 1\) is inserted into a charged capacitor isolated from the charging battery, the electrostatic energy stored in the capacitor decreases.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: जब नियत वोल्टता \(V\) की बैटरी से जुड़े संधारित्र में परावैद्युतांक \(K > 1\) की एक परावैद्युत पट्टिका प्रविष्ट की जाती है, तो संधारित्र में संचित स्थिर-वैद्युत ऊर्जा घट जाती है।

कथन II: जब आवेशन बैटरी से अलग किए गए एक आवेशित संधारित्र में परावैद्युतांक \(K > 1\) की एक परावैद्युत पट्टिका प्रविष्ट की जाती है, तो संधारित्र में संचित स्थिर-वैद्युत ऊर्जा घट जाती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
When a capacitor remains connected to a battery, the potential difference \(V\) across the plates remains strictly constant. Upon inserting a dielectric slab of constant \(K\), the capacitance increases from \(C_0\) to \(C = K C_0\). The electrostatic energy stored is given by: \[ U = \frac{1}{2} C V^2 = \frac{1}{2} (K C_0) V^2 = K U_0 \] Since \(K > 1\), the stored energy increases by a factor of \(K\), not decreases. (The battery supplies energy \(\Delta W_{\text{batt}} = \Delta Q \cdot V = (K-1)C_0 V^2\) during this process). Therefore, Statement I is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
When the capacitor is disconnected from the battery before the dielectric is inserted, the capacitor is electrically isolated. By the law of conservation of charge, the charge on the plates remains constant (\(Q = Q_0\)). The capacitance increases to \(C = K C_0\). The electrostatic energy stored is: \[ U = \frac{Q_0^2}{2C} = \frac{Q_0^2}{2(K C_0)} = \frac{U_0}{K} \] Since \(K > 1\), the stored energy decreases to \(1/K\) times its initial value. (The lost electrostatic energy is converted into mechanical work done by the electrostatic attractive force pulling the dielectric slab into the plates). Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Conclusion
Statement I is incorrect because energy increases when the battery remains connected, while Statement II is correct because energy decreases when the capacitor is isolated.

Final Conceptual Answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
जब संधारित्र बैटरी से जुड़ा रहता है, तो पट्टिकाओं के बीच विभवांतर \(V\) नियत रहता है। परावैद्युतांक \(K\) की पट्टिका प्रविष्ट करने पर धारिता \(C_0\) से बढ़कर \(C = K C_0\) हो जाती है। संचित स्थिर-वैद्युत ऊर्जा निम्न है: \[ U = \frac{1}{2} C V^2 = \frac{1}{2} (K C_0) V^2 = K U_0 \] चूँकि \(K > 1\) है, अतः संचित ऊर्जा \(K\) गुना बढ़ जाती है, घटती नहीं है। (इस प्रक्रिया के दौरान बैटरी अतिरिक्त ऊर्जा की आपूर्ति करती है)। इसलिए, कथन I गलत है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
जब परावैद्युत रखने से पहले संधारित्र को बैटरी से हटा दिया जाता है, तो संधारित्र विलगित (आइसोलेटेड) हो जाता है। आवेश संरक्षण के नियम से, पट्टिकाओं पर कुल आवेश नियत रहता है (\(Q = Q_0\))। धारिता बढ़कर \(C = K C_0\) हो जाती है। संचित स्थिर-वैद्युत ऊर्जा: \[ U = \frac{Q_0^2}{2C} = \frac{Q_0^2}{2(K C_0)} = \frac{U_0}{K} \] चूँकि \(K > 1\) है, अतः संचित ऊर्जा घटकर अपने प्रारंभिक मान का \(1/K\) रह जाती है। (यह ऊर्जा ह्रास परावैद्युत पट्टिका को पट्टिकाओं के बीच खींचने में स्थिर-वैद्युत आकर्षण बल द्वारा किए गए कार्य में परिवर्तित हो जाता है)। इसलिए, कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: निष्कर्ष
कथन I गलत है क्योंकि बैटरी जुड़े रहने पर ऊर्जा बढ़ती है, जबकि कथन II सही है क्योंकि विलगित रहने पर संचित ऊर्जा घटती है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: कथन I गलत है लेकिन कथन II सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH02_ST2_Q08 - Electrostatic shielding and fields inside and outside a conducting cavity

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In electrostatic equilibrium, an empty cavity within an uncharged closed conductor is completely shielded from any external electrostatic fields regardless of their strength.

Statement II: In electrostatic equilibrium, the electrostatic potential is uniform throughout the entire volume of a conductor, including any empty cavity inside it, and is equal to the potential on its surface.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: स्थिर-वैद्युत साम्यावस्था में, एक अनावेशित बंद चालक के भीतर स्थित एक रिक्त गुहिका (कैविटी) किसी भी बाह्य स्थिर-वैद्युत क्षेत्र से, चाहे उसकी तीव्रता कितनी भी हो, पूर्णतः परिरक्षित (शील्डेड) रहती है।

कथन II: स्थिर-वैद्युत साम्यावस्था में, चालक के संपूर्ण आयतन में, जिसमें इसके अंदर की कोई भी रिक्त गुहिका शामिल है, स्थिर-वैद्युत विभव एकसमान होता है और इसके पृष्ठ के विभव के बराबर होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
By Gauss's law and the properties of conductors in electrostatic equilibrium, charges on the conductor redistribute over the outer surface in such a way that the electric field inside the conducting material is identically zero. Because there is no charge enclosed within an empty cavity (\(q_{\text{enclosed}} = 0\)), the electric field inside the cavity is strictly zero (\(\mathbf{E} = 0\)), completely shielding any object inside the cavity from external electric fields. This phenomenon is known as electrostatic shielding. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
Since \(\mathbf{E} = 0\) everywhere inside the conductor material and throughout the empty cavity, the electric potential gradient vanishes identically: \[ \mathbf{E} = -\nabla V = 0 \implies V = \text{constant} \] Thus, no work is done in moving a test charge between any two points within the conductor or within the cavity. Consequently, the electrostatic potential is constant throughout the entire volume of the conductor and its empty cavity, having precisely the same numerical value as the surface potential. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Conclusion
Both statements accurately state fundamental theorems regarding electrostatic shielding and potential constancy inside a conducting body.

Final Conceptual Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
गाउस के नियम और स्थिर-वैद्युत साम्यावस्था में चालकों के गुणों के अनुसार, चालक पर उपस्थित आवेश उसके बाह्य पृष्ठ पर इस प्रकार पुनर्वितरित होते हैं कि चालक पदार्थ के भीतर विद्युत क्षेत्र सर्वत्र शून्य हो जाता है। चूँकि रिक्त गुहिका के भीतर कोई आवेश परिबद्ध नहीं होता है (\(q_{\text{enclosed}} = 0\)), अतः गुहिका के अंदर विद्युत क्षेत्र पूर्णतः शून्य (\(\mathbf{E} = 0\)) रहता है, जिससे गुहिका के अंदर की कोई भी वस्तु बाह्य विद्युत क्षेत्रों से पूरी तरह परिरक्षित रहती है। इस परिघटना को स्थिर-वैद्युत परिरक्षण कहते हैं। अतः, कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
चूँकि चालक पदार्थ के भीतर तथा रिक्त गुहिका के संपूर्ण आयतन में सर्वत्र \(\mathbf{E} = 0\) होता है, अतः विभव प्रवणता शून्य हो जाती है: \[ \mathbf{E} = -\nabla V = 0 \implies V = \text{नियत} \] अतः, चालक के भीतर या गुहिका के भीतर किन्हीं दो बिंदुओं के बीच परीक्षण आवेश को ले जाने में कोई कार्य नहीं किया जाता है। फलस्वरूप, स्थिर-वैद्युत विभव चालक के संपूर्ण आयतन तथा उसकी रिक्त गुहिका में एकसमान रहता है और इसका मान ठीक पृष्ठ पर विभव के बराबर होता है। अतः, कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: निष्कर्ष
दोनों कथन स्थिर-वैद्युत परिरक्षण तथा चालक के भीतर विभव की स्थिरता के मूलभूत सिद्धांतों का सही वर्णन करते हैं।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: दोनों कथन I और कथन II सही हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH02_ST3_Q01 - Electrostatic field and potential characteristics of a point charge

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the electrostatic field and potential of a point charge:

Statement I: The electric potential due to an isolated positive point charge decreases monotonically as the distance from the charge increases.

Statement II: The electric field lines of an isolated point charge are radial lines that are everywhere perpendicular to the concentric spherical equipotential surfaces.

Statement III: The electrostatic potential at infinity due to any finite localized charge configuration is conventionally taken to be non-zero and positive.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

किसी बिंदु आवेश के स्थिर-वैद्युत क्षेत्र और विभव के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: एक विलगित धनात्मक बिंदु आवेश के कारण स्थिर-वैद्युत विभव, आवेश से दूरी बढ़ने पर निरंतर घटता जाता है।

कथन II: एक विलगित बिंदु आवेश की विद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाएं त्रिज्य रेखाएं होती हैं जो संकेंद्री गोलीय समविभव पृष्ठों के सर्वत्र लंबवत होती हैं।

कथन III: किसी भी परिमित स्थानीकृत आवेश विन्यास के कारण अनंत पर स्थिर-वैद्युत विभव को परिपाटी के अनुसार अशून्य और धनात्मक माना जाता है।

उपर्युक्त दिए गए कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
The electrostatic potential at a distance \(r\) from an isolated positive point charge \(Q > 0\) in vacuum is given by \(V(r) = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{Q}{r}\). As the distance \(r\) increases, the quantity \(1/r\) decreases strictly, meaning \(V(r)\) decreases monotonically toward zero as \(r \to \infty\). Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
For a point charge, the electric field is purely radial, directed along \(\hat{\mathbf{r}}\). The surfaces over which the potential \(V(r)\) is constant are concentric spheres centered on the charge. The outward normal to any concentric sphere at any point is along the radial vector \(\hat{\mathbf{r}}\). Because \(\mathbf{E} = -\nabla V\), the electric field lines are everywhere perpendicular to the equipotential surfaces. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
By universal scientific convention, the reference point for electrostatic potential due to a localized charge distribution is chosen at infinity, where \(V(\infty) = 0\), not a non-zero or positive value. This reference definition ensures that the potential at any finite point equals the work done in bringing a unit positive charge from infinity. Therefore, Statement III is incorrect.

Step 4: Conclusion
Statements I and II are correct, whereas Statement III is incorrect.

Final Conceptual Answer: Statement I and Statement II only

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
निर्वात में एक विलगित धनात्मक बिंदु आवेश \(Q > 0\) से दूरी \(r\) पर स्थिर-वैद्युत विभव का सूत्र \(V(r) = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{Q}{r}\) होता है। जैसे-जैसे दूरी \(r\) बढ़ती है, पद \(1/r\) का मान निरंतर घटता है, जिसका अर्थ है कि \(r \to \infty\) होने पर \(V(r)\) निरंतर शून्य की ओर घटता जाता है। अतः, कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
एक बिंदु आवेश के लिए विद्युत क्षेत्र पूर्णतः त्रिज्य (रेडियल) होता है, जो \(\hat{\mathbf{r}}\) के अनुदिश निर्दिष्ट होता है। वे पृष्ठ जिन पर विभव \(V(r)\) नियत रहता है, आवेश पर केंद्रित संकेंद्री गोले होते हैं। किसी भी संकेंद्री गोले पर अभिलंब सदैव त्रिज्य सदिश \(\hat{\mathbf{r}}\) के अनुदिश होता है। चूँकि \(\mathbf{E} = -\nabla V\) होता है, अतः विद्युत क्षेत्र रेखाएं समविभव पृष्ठों के सर्वत्र लंबवत होती हैं। अतः, कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
सार्वभौमिक वैज्ञानिक परिपाटी के अनुसार, स्थानीकृत आवेश वितरण के लिए स्थिर-वैद्युत विभव का निर्देश बिंदु अनंत पर चुना जाता है, जहाँ \(V(\infty) = 0\) लिया जाता है, न कि कोई अशून्य या धनात्मक मान। यह चयन सुनिश्चित करता है कि किसी परिमित बिंदु पर विभव एकांक धनात्मक आवेश को अनंत से लाने में किए गए कार्य के बराबर हो। अतः, कथन III गलत है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
कथन I और II सही हैं, जबकि कथन III गलत है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: केवल कथन I और कथन II (Statement I and Statement II only)

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH02_ST3_Q02 - Electrostatic properties of metallic solid conductors in equilibrium

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding a solid metallic conductor in electrostatic equilibrium:

Statement I: Any excess charge supplied to the conductor distributes uniformly throughout its interior volume element.

Statement II: The electrostatic potential is constant throughout the entire volume of the conductor and equals the potential on its surface.

Statement III: The electrostatic field just outside the surface of the charged conductor is perpendicular to the surface with magnitude \(\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\), where \(\sigma\) is the local surface charge density.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

स्थिर-वैद्युत साम्यावस्था में एक ठोस धात्विक चालक के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: चालक को दिया गया कोई भी अतिरिक्त आवेश इसके आंतरिक आयतन अल्पांश में एकसमान रूप से वितरित हो जाता है।

कथन II: चालक के संपूर्ण आयतन में स्थिर-वैद्युत विभव नियत रहता है और इसका मान इसके पृष्ठ पर विभव के बराबर होता है।

कथन III: आवेशित चालक के पृष्ठ के ठीक बाहर स्थिर-वैद्युत क्षेत्र पृष्ठ के लंबवत होता है तथा इसका परिमाण \(\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\) होता है, जहाँ \(\sigma\) स्थानीय पृष्ठ आवेश घनत्व है।

उपर्युक्त दिए गए कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
In electrostatic equilibrium, there are no moving currents, which requires the electrostatic field inside the conductor to be identically zero (\(\mathbf{E} = 0\)). By Gauss's law, any arbitrary Gaussian surface drawn inside the conductor encloses zero net flux, which proves that the enclosed net charge is strictly zero everywhere in the interior (\(\rho = 0\)). Hence, any excess charge resides entirely on the outer surface of the conductor, never in its interior volume. Therefore, Statement I is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
Because \(\mathbf{E} = 0\) everywhere inside the conductor and has no tangential component along the surface, the work done in moving a test charge between any two interior or surface points is identically zero (\(dV = -\mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{r} = 0\)). Thus, the entire conductor is an equipotential body: the potential is constant throughout its interior and matches its surface value. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
Applying Gauss's law to a small cylindrical pillbox half-submerged at the surface of the conductor, the inner end face experiences \(\mathbf{E} = 0\) while the outer end face of area \(\delta S\) receives flux \(E \delta S\). Setting \(E \delta S = \frac{\sigma \delta S}{\varepsilon_0}\) gives \(E = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\) along the normal unit vector \(\hat{\mathbf{n}}\). Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
Statements II and III are correct, whereas Statement I is incorrect.

Final Conceptual Answer: Statement II and Statement III only

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
स्थिर-वैद्युत साम्यावस्था में कोई गतिमान धारा नहीं होती, जिसके लिए चालक के भीतर स्थिर-वैद्युत क्षेत्र का पूर्णतः शून्य (\(\mathbf{E} = 0\)) होना आवश्यक है। गाउस के नियम से, चालक के भीतर खींचे गए किसी भी स्वेच्छ गाउसीय पृष्ठ से परिबद्ध कुल फ्लक्स शून्य होता है, जो सिद्ध करता है कि आंतरिक भाग में सर्वत्र कुल आवेश शून्य होता है (\(\rho = 0\))। अतः, कोई भी अतिरिक्त आवेश पूरी तरह से चालक के बाह्य पृष्ठ पर रहता है, कभी भी आंतरिक आयतन में नहीं। इसलिए, कथन I गलत है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
चूँकि चालक के भीतर सर्वत्र \(\mathbf{E} = 0\) होता है तथा पृष्ठ के अनुदिश कोई स्पर्शरेखीय घटक नहीं होता है, अतः किन्हीं दो आंतरिक अथवा पृष्ठीय बिंदुओं के बीच परीक्षण आवेश को ले जाने में किया गया कार्य शून्य होता है (\(dV = -\mathbf{E} \cdot d\mathbf{r} = 0\))। इस प्रकार, संपूर्ण चालक एक समविभव पिंड होता है: विभव इसके संपूर्ण आंतरिक भाग में नियत रहता है तथा पृष्ठ पर इसके मान के बराबर होता है। अतः, कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
चालक के पृष्ठ पर आधे डूबे हुए एक छोटे बेलनाकार पिल-बॉक्स पर गाउस का नियम लागू करने पर, आंतरिक सिरे पर \(\mathbf{E} = 0\) होता है जबकि बाह्य सिरे (क्षेत्रफल \(\delta S\)) से फ्लक्स \(E \delta S\) प्राप्त होता है। समीकरण \(E \delta S = \frac{\sigma \delta S}{\varepsilon_0}\) से प्राप्त होता है कि \(E = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\), जो अभिलंब इकाई सदिश \(\hat{\mathbf{n}}\) के अनुदिश होता है। अतः, कथन III सही है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
कथन II और III सही हैं, जबकि कथन I गलत है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: केवल कथन II और कथन III (Statement II and Statement III only)

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH02_ST3_Q03 - Capacitance and energy relations for parallel plate capacitors

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding parallel plate capacitors and their combinations:

Statement I: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with vacuum between the plates is directly proportional to the plate area \(A\) and inversely proportional to the plate separation \(d\).

Statement II: When two identical capacitors of capacitance \(C\) are connected in parallel, the equivalent capacitance of the combination is \(2C\).

Statement III: The electrostatic energy stored in a capacitor of capacitance \(C\) carrying charge \(Q\) is given by \(U = \frac{Q^2}{2C}\).

Which of the statements given above are correct?

समांतर पट्टिका संधारित्रों और उनके संयोजनों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: पट्टिकाओं के बीच निर्वात वाले समांतर पट्टिका संधारित्र की धारिता पट्टिका क्षेत्रफल \(A\) के अनुक्रमानुपाती तथा पट्टिका पृथक्करण \(d\) के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है।

कथन II: जब धारिता \(C\) वाले दो समरूप संधारित्र पार्श्वक्रम (समानांतर) में जोड़े जाते हैं, तो संयोजन की तुल्य धारिता \(2C\) होती है।

कथन III: आवेश \(Q\) धारण करने वाले धारिता \(C\) के संधारित्र में संचित स्थिर-वैद्युत ऊर्जा \(U = \frac{Q^2}{2C}\) द्वारा दी जाती है।

उपर्युक्त दिए गए कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
For a parallel plate capacitor with vacuum between plates of area \(A\) separated by distance \(d\), the electric field is \(E = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0} = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0 A}\) and the potential difference is \(V = E d = \frac{Q d}{\varepsilon_0 A}\). The capacitance is: \[ C = \frac{Q}{V} = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d} \] Thus, \(C\) is directly proportional to \(A\) and inversely proportional to \(d\). Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
In a parallel combination, the same potential difference \(V\) is applied across both capacitors. The total charge is \(Q_{\text{total}} = Q_1 + Q_2 = C V + C V = 2C V\). The effective capacitance is: \[ C_{\text{eq}} = \frac{Q_{\text{total}}}{V} = C + C = 2C \] Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
The work done in charging a capacitor by transferring charge increments \(dq'\) at instantaneous potential \(V' = q'/C\) is given by: \[ U = \int_0^Q \frac{q'}{C} dq' = \frac{Q^2}{2C} \] Using \(Q = CV\), this can also be expressed as \(\frac{1}{2}CV^2\) or \(\frac{1}{2}QV\). Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
All three statements are conceptually and analytically correct.

Final Conceptual Answer: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
क्षेत्रफल \(A\) तथा पृथक्करण दूरी \(d\) वाली निर्वातित समांतर पट्टिकाओं के लिए विद्युत क्षेत्र \(E = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0} = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0 A}\) तथा विभवांतर \(V = E d = \frac{Q d}{\varepsilon_0 A}\) होता है। संधारित्र की धारिता: \[ C = \frac{Q}{V} = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d} \] अतः, \(C\) क्षेत्रफल \(A\) के अनुक्रमानुपाती तथा दूरी \(d\) के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है। इसलिए, कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
समानांतर (पार्श्व) संयोजन में, दोनों संधारित्रों पर समान विभवांतर \(V\) लागू होता है। कुल आवेश \(Q_{\text{total}} = Q_1 + Q_2 = C V + C V = 2C V\) होता है। तुल्य धारिता: \[ C_{\text{eq}} = \frac{Q_{\text{total}}}{V} = C + C = 2C \] इसलिए, कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
तात्कालिक विभव \(V' = q'/C\) पर आवेश अल्पांश \(dq'\) को स्थानांतरित करके संधारित्र को आवेशित करने में किया गया कार्य: \[ U = \int_0^Q \frac{q'}{C} dq' = \frac{Q^2}{2C} \] समीकरण \(Q = CV\) का उपयोग करके इसे \(\frac{1}{2}CV^2\) या \(\frac{1}{2}QV\) के रूप में भी लिखा जा सकता है। इसलिए, कथन III सही है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
तीनों कथन वैचारिक और विश्लेषणात्मक रूप से सही हैं।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: कथन I, कथन II और कथन III (Statement I, Statement II and Statement III)

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH02_ST3_Q04 - Dielectric insertion in isolated and battery-connected parallel plate capacitors

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the effect of inserting a dielectric slab of dielectric constant \(K > 1\) into a parallel plate capacitor:

Statement I: Dielectric polarization produces induced surface charges that generate an internal electric field opposing the applied external field, thereby reducing the net field inside the dielectric to \(\frac{E_0}{K}\).

Statement II: If a capacitor is charged to voltage \(V_0\) and then disconnected from the battery, inserting the dielectric slab increases the total charge residing on the conducting plates.

Statement III: If the capacitor remains continuously connected to a battery of voltage \(V_0\) while the dielectric slab is inserted, the potential difference across the plates remains \(V_0\) while the electrostatic energy stored increases by a factor of \(K\).

Which of the statements given above are correct?

एक समांतर पट्टिका संधारित्र में परावैद्युतांक \(K > 1\) की एक परावैद्युत पट्टिका प्रविष्ट करने के प्रभाव के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: परावैद्युत ध्रुवण के कारण प्रेरित पृष्ठीय आवेश उत्पन्न होते हैं जो अनुप्रयुक्त बाह्य क्षेत्र का विरोध करने वाला एक आंतरिक विद्युत क्षेत्र उत्पन्न करते हैं, जिससे परावैद्युत के अंदर कुल विद्युत क्षेत्र घटकर \(\frac{E_0}{K}\) रह जाता है।

कथन II: यदि एक संधारित्र को वोल्टता \(V_0\) तक आवेशित किया जाता है और फिर बैटरी से अलग कर दिया जाता है, तो परावैद्युत पट्टिका डालने से चालक पट्टिकाओं पर उपस्थित कुल आवेश बढ़ जाता है।

कथन III: यदि परावैद्युत पट्टिका डालते समय संधारित्र वोल्टता \(V_0\) की बैटरी से लगातार जुड़ा रहता है, तो पट्टिकाओं के बीच विभवांतर \(V_0\) बना रहता है जबकि संचित स्थिर-वैद्युत ऊर्जा \(K\) गुना बढ़ जाती है।

उपर्युक्त दिए गए कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
In an external electric field \(\mathbf{E}_0\), molecular dipoles in the dielectric align, producing induced surface charge densities \(\pm \sigma_p\). These bound charges set up an internal opposing electric field \(\mathbf{E}_p\). The resultant electric field inside the linear isotropic dielectric is \(E = E_0 - E_p = \frac{E_0}{K}\). Because \(K > 1\), the net electric field inside the dielectric is reduced by a factor of \(K\). Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
When the battery is disconnected prior to inserting the dielectric, the plates form an isolated system. Charge conservation dictates that no charge can flow onto or off the conducting plates (\(Q = Q_0 = \text{constant}\)). Inserting the dielectric increases capacitance to \(C = K C_0\) and decreases voltage to \(V = V_0 / K\), but does not alter the plate charge \(Q_0\). Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
When the capacitor remains connected to a battery of fixed potential difference \(V_0\), the voltage across the plates is held fixed at \(V = V_0\). The capacitance increases to \(C = K C_0\). The initial stored electrostatic energy was \(U_0 = \frac{1}{2} C_0 V_0^2\), and the new stored energy is: \[ U = \frac{1}{2} C V_0^2 = \frac{1}{2} (K C_0) V_0^2 = K U_0 \] Thus, the stored energy increases by a factor of \(K\). Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
Statements I and III are correct, whereas Statement II is incorrect.

Final Conceptual Answer: Statement I and Statement III only

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
बाह्य विद्युत क्षेत्र \(\mathbf{E}_0\) में, परावैद्युत के आणविक द्विध्रुव संरेखित हो जाते हैं, जिससे प्रेरित पृष्ठीय आवेश घनत्व \(\pm \sigma_p\) उत्पन्न होता है। ये परिबद्ध आवेश एक आंतरिक विपरीत विद्युत क्षेत्र \(\mathbf{E}_p\) स्थापित करते हैं। रैखिक समदैशिक परावैद्युत के अंदर परिणामी विद्युत क्षेत्र \(E = E_0 - E_p = \frac{E_0}{K}\) होता है। चूँकि \(K > 1\) है, अतः परावैद्युत के भीतर कुल विद्युत क्षेत्र \(K\) के गुणक से घट जाता है। अतः, कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
परावैद्युत रखने से पहले जब बैटरी को हटा दिया जाता है, तो पट्टिकाएं एक विलगित निकाय बन जाती हैं। आवेश संरक्षण के नियमानुसार, चालक पट्टिकाओं पर न तो आवेश आ सकता है और न ही जा सकता है (\(Q = Q_0 = \text{नियत}\))। परावैद्युत रखने पर धारिता बढ़कर \(C = K C_0\) हो जाती है तथा विभवांतर घटकर \(V = V_0 / K\) रह जाता है, परंतु पट्टिका आवेश \(Q_0\) अपरिवर्तित रहता है। अतः, कथन II गलत है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
जब संधारित्र निश्चित विभवांतर \(V_0\) वाली बैटरी से लगातार जुड़ा रहता है, तो पट्टिकाओं के बीच वोल्टता \(V = V_0\) पर नियत रहती है। धारिता बढ़कर \(C = K C_0\) हो जाती है। प्रारंभिक संचित स्थिर-वैद्युत ऊर्जा \(U_0 = \frac{1}{2} C_0 V_0^2\) थी, तथा नई संचित ऊर्जा निम्न होगी: \[ U = \frac{1}{2} C V_0^2 = \frac{1}{2} (K C_0) V_0^2 = K U_0 \] अतः, संचित ऊर्जा \(K\) गुना बढ़ जाती है। अतः, कथन III सही है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
कथन I और III सही हैं, जबकि कथन II गलत है।

अंतिम वैचारिक उत्तर: केवल कथन I और कथन III (Statement I and Statement III only)

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q01 - Physical quantities and their SI units

questiontext.text:
Match the physical quantities in List-I with their corresponding SI units in List-II:

List-IList-II
(A) Electrostatic potential(I) \(\text{C}\cdot\text{m}^{-2}\)
(B) Capacitance(II) \(\text{J}\cdot\text{m}^{-3}\)
(C) Electric polarisation(III) \(\text{V}\)
(D) Electrostatic energy density(IV) \(\text{F}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Electrostatic potential, capacitance, polarisation, and electrostatic energy density are standard physical quantities defined in electrostatics.

Step 2: Analysis of First Pair
Electrostatic potential is the work done per unit test charge, \(V = \frac{W}{q}\), with SI unit of volt (\(\text{V}\), equivalent to \(\text{J}\cdot\text{C}^{-1}\)).

Step 3: Analysis of Second Pair
Capacitance is the ratio of stored charge to potential difference, \(C = \frac{Q}{V}\), with SI unit of farad (\(\text{F}\), equivalent to \(\text{C}\cdot\text{V}^{-1}\)).

Step 4: Analysis of Third Pair
Electric polarisation represents the dipole moment per unit volume, \(\mathbf{P} = \frac{\mathbf{p}}{\Delta v}\), having the SI unit of coulomb per square metre (\(\text{C}\cdot\text{m}^{-2}\)).

Step 5: Analysis of Fourth Pair
Electrostatic energy density is the energy stored per unit volume of the electric field, \(u = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2\), which has the SI unit of joule per cubic metre (\(\text{J}\cdot\text{m}^{-3}\)).

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Matching each physical quantity with its unit yields: Electrostatic potential corresponds to \(\text{V}\); Capacitance corresponds to \(\text{F}\); Electric polarisation corresponds to \(\text{C}\cdot\text{m}^{-2}\); Electrostatic energy density corresponds to \(\text{J}\cdot\text{m}^{-3}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q02 - Electrostatic field and potential distance dependence

questiontext.text:
Match each electrostatic configuration in List-I with its characteristic spatial dependence in List-II:

List-IList-II
(A) Electric potential due to an isolated point charge(I) Zero everywhere
(B) Electric field magnitude due to an isolated point charge(II) Varies inversely as \(r\)
(C) Electric potential on the equatorial plane of an electric dipole(III) Varies inversely as \(r^2\)
(D) Electric field magnitude of a short dipole at large axial distance(IV) Varies inversely as \(r^3\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The distance dependence of electric fields and potentials depends on the multipole order of the source charge distribution.

Step 2: Analysis of First Pair
For an isolated monopole point charge \(q\), the electric potential is \(V(r) = \frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r}\), which varies inversely with distance as \(1/r\).

Step 3: Analysis of Second Pair
The electric field of an isolated point charge is governed by Coulomb's law, \(E(r) = \frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}\), exhibiting an inverse-square dependence as \(1/r^2\).

Step 4: Analysis of Third Pair
For an electric dipole, the potential at any point is \(V(r, \theta) = \frac{p\cos\theta}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}\). On the equatorial plane, \(\theta = 90^\circ\) and \(\cos 90^\circ = 0\), meaning the potential is identically zero everywhere on this plane.

Step 5: Analysis of Fourth Pair
Along the axial line of a short electric dipole, the electric field at large distance (\(r \gg a\)) is \(E = \frac{2p}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^3}\), falling off inversely as the cube of distance, \(1/r^3\).

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Matching each configuration with its spatial variation yields: Electric potential of a point charge corresponds to varying inversely as \(r\); Electric field of a point charge corresponds to varying inversely as \(r^2\); Potential on dipole equatorial plane corresponds to zero everywhere; Electric field of a short dipole on axis corresponds to varying inversely as \(r^3\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q03 - Capacitor parameters under dielectric insertion

questiontext.text:
A parallel plate capacitor with initial parameters \(C_0\), \(Q_0\), \(V_0\), and \(U_0\) is filled with a dielectric slab of constant \(K > 1\). Match the condition in List-I with the resulting parameter in List-II:

List-IList-II
(A) Capacitance of the capacitor with the dielectric slab present(I) Decreases to \(V_0 / K\)
(B) Potential difference across the plates when dielectric is inserted with battery disconnected(II) Increases to \(K C_0\)
(C) Charge on the plates when dielectric is inserted with battery remaining connected(III) Decreases to \(U_0 / K\)
(D) Electrostatic energy stored when dielectric is inserted with battery disconnected(IV) Increases to \(K Q_0\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor completely filled with a dielectric of constant \(K\) becomes \(C = K C_0\), irrespective of external circuit connections.

Step 2: Analysis of First Pair
The capacitance increases from \(C_0\) to \(K C_0\) due to dielectric polarization neutralizing a fraction of the surface charge field.

Step 3: Analysis of Second Pair
When the charging battery is disconnected prior to inserting the slab, the plate charge remains isolated and conserved at \(Q = Q_0\). Consequently, the potential difference becomes \(V = \frac{Q_0}{C} = \frac{Q_0}{K C_0} = \frac{V_0}{K}\), decreasing by a factor of \(K\).

Step 4: Analysis of Third Pair
When the battery remains connected, the potential difference is actively fixed at \(V = V_0\). The new stored charge is \(Q = C V_0 = (K C_0) V_0 = K Q_0\), increasing by a factor of \(K\).

Step 5: Analysis of Fourth Pair
With the battery disconnected, the stored electrostatic energy is \(U = \frac{Q_0^2}{2C} = \frac{Q_0^2}{2 K C_0} = \frac{U_0}{K}\), decreasing by a factor of \(K\) as electrostatic work is done by the field on the slab.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Matching each scenario with its resulting value yields: Capacitance with dielectric corresponds to increasing to \(K C_0\); Potential difference with battery disconnected corresponds to decreasing to \(V_0 / K\); Charge with battery connected corresponds to increasing to \(K Q_0\); Stored energy with battery disconnected corresponds to decreasing to \(U_0 / K\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q04 - Electrostatic states of conductors and dipoles

questiontext.text:
Match each electrostatic system in List-I with its physical state or property in List-II:

List-IList-II
(A) Charge-free cavity inside an arbitrarily shaped conductor(I) Electric field is \(\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\hat{\mathbf{n}}\) normal to the surface
(B) Outer surface of a charged conductor with local surface charge density \(\sigma\)(II) Torque is zero and potential energy is at its minimum of \(-pE\)
(C) Electric dipole aligned parallel to a uniform electric field(III) Electric field is strictly zero regardless of external fields
(D) Electric dipole aligned perpendicular to a uniform electric field(IV) Torque is maximum at \(pE\) and potential energy is zero

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Electrostatic equilibrium in conductors enforces specific boundary conditions, and the potential energy of a dipole in an external field is given by \(U = -\mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{E} = -pE\cos\theta\) with torque \(\boldsymbol{\tau} = \mathbf{p} \times \mathbf{E}\).

Step 2: Analysis of First Pair
By the principle of electrostatic shielding, any empty cavity within a conductor remains completely shielded from external electrical fields, ensuring that the electric field inside the cavity is strictly zero.

Step 3: Analysis of Second Pair
By Gauss's law applied across the conducting boundary, the electrostatic field just outside a charged conductor is \(E = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\), oriented strictly perpendicular to the conducting surface.

Step 4: Analysis of Third Pair
When a dipole is aligned parallel to the field (\(\theta = 0^\circ\)), \(\sin 0^\circ = 0\) so the torque is zero, and \(\cos 0^\circ = 1\) so the potential energy reaches its global minimum, \(U_{\min} = -pE\) (stable equilibrium).

Step 5: Analysis of Fourth Pair
When a dipole is oriented perpendicular to the field (\(\theta = 90^\circ\)), the torque reaches its maximum value of \(\tau = pE\sin 90^\circ = pE\), while the potential energy is \(U = -pE\cos 90^\circ = 0\).

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Matching each system with its state yields: Charge-free cavity corresponds to electric field strictly zero; Outer surface of conductor corresponds to field of \(\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\hat{\mathbf{n}}\); Dipole parallel to field corresponds to zero torque and minimum energy \(-pE\); Dipole perpendicular to field corresponds to maximum torque \(pE\) and zero energy.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q01 - Electric potential due to a point charge

questiontext.text: What is the electrostatic potential at a point located at a distance of \(9\text{ cm}\) from an isolated positive point charge of \(4 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}\)? (Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: charge \(q = 4 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}\), distance \(r = 9\text{ cm} = 0.09\text{ m}\), and electrostatic constant \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The electrostatic potential is defined with the reference point at infinity where \(V(\infty) = 0\). The medium is free space (vacuum).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The electric potential due to a point charge at distance \(r\) is given by:\[V = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q}{r}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given numerical values:\[V = \left(9 \times 10^9\right) \times \frac{4 \times 10^{-7}}{0.09}\]Simplify the numerator and denominator:\[V = \frac{3600}{0.09} = 4.0 \times 10^4\text{ V}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The calculated potential has standard units of volts (\(\text{V}\)) and positive sign consistent with a positive source charge. Thus, the electric potential is \(4.0 \times 10^4\text{ V}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q02 - Work done moving charge from infinity

questiontext.text: How much work is done by an external force in bringing a test charge of \(2 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}\) from infinity to a point where the electric potential is \(4 \times 10^4\text{ V}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: charge brought \(q = 2 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}\), potential at the final point \(V = 4 \times 10^4\text{ V}\), and initial potential at infinity \(V_\infty = 0\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The motion is without acceleration (infinitesimally slow), so work done by the external agent equals the increase in electrostatic potential energy.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The work done in moving a charge from infinity to a point of potential \(V\) is:\[W = q \Delta V = q(V - V_\infty) = q V\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the known values into the equation:\[W = \left(2 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}\right) \times \left(4 \times 10^4\text{ V}\right) = 8.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ J}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The unit \(\text{C}\cdot\text{V} = \text{J}\). The work done is positive because work is performed against the electrostatic field. Hence, the work done is \(8.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q03 - Capacitance of parallel plate air capacitor

questiontext.text: In a parallel plate air capacitor, each plate has an area of \(6.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^2\) and the separation between the plates is \(3.0\text{ mm}\). Taking \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2\text{N}^{-1}\text{m}^{-2}\), what is the capacitance of the capacitor?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: plate area \(A = 6.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^2\), plate separation \(d = 3.0\text{ mm} = 3.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}\), and permittivity of free space \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ F/m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Assume uniform electric field between the plates, neglecting fringe effects near the plate edges.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with air or vacuum dielectric is given by:\[C = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given numbers:\[C = \frac{8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 6.0 \times 10^{-3}}{3.0 \times 10^{-3}} = 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 2 = 17.7 \times 10^{-12}\text{ F} = 17.7\text{ pF}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The resulting capacitance is \(17.7\text{ pF}\), which conforms to standard laboratory orders of magnitude for parallel plate capacitors.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q04 - Equivalent capacitance of identical series capacitors

questiontext.text: Three identical capacitors, each of capacitance \(9\text{ pF}\), are connected in series. What is the total equivalent capacitance of the combination?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: three capacitors connected in series, each having capacitance \(C_1 = C_2 = C_3 = 9\text{ pF}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In a series combination, the charge on each capacitor is identical, and the total potential difference is the sum of the potential differences across each capacitor.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The formula for the equivalent capacitance \(C_{eq}\) of three capacitors in series is:\[\frac{1}{C_{eq}} = \frac{1}{C_1} + \frac{1}{C_2} + \frac{1}{C_3}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the identical capacitance values:\[\frac{1}{C_{eq}} = \frac{1}{9} + \frac{1}{9} + \frac{1}{9} = \frac{3}{9} = \frac{1}{3}\text{ pF}^{-1}\]Inverting both sides:\[C_{eq} = 3\text{ pF}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The equivalent series capacitance is less than the smallest individual capacitance (\(3\text{ pF} < 9\text{ pF}\)), confirming consistency. The equivalent capacitance is \(3\text{ pF}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q05 - Equivalent capacitance of parallel capacitor combination

questiontext.text: Three capacitors of capacitances \(2\text{ pF}\), \(3\text{ pF}\), and \(4\text{ pF}\) are connected in parallel. What is the total equivalent capacitance of this combination?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: three capacitors connected in parallel with individual capacitances \(C_1 = 2\text{ pF}\), \(C_2 = 3\text{ pF}\), and \(C_3 = 4\text{ pF}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In a parallel connection, the potential difference across each capacitor is the same, and the total charge is the sum of the charges on each capacitor.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The equivalent capacitance \(C_p\) for capacitors in parallel is the direct sum:\[C_p = C_1 + C_2 + C_3\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given numerical values:\[C_p = 2\text{ pF} + 3\text{ pF} + 4\text{ pF} = 9\text{ pF}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The equivalent capacitance in parallel is strictly greater than any individual capacitor (\(9\text{ pF} > 4\text{ pF}\)). Thus, the total capacitance is \(9\text{ pF}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q06 - Electrostatic energy stored in a capacitor

questiontext.text: A \(12\text{ pF}\) capacitor is connected to a \(50\text{ V}\) battery. How much electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: capacitance \(C = 12\text{ pF} = 12 \times 10^{-12}\text{ F}\), and potential difference \(V = 50\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Assume ideal capacitor with negligible dielectric loss and steady state conditions.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The electrostatic energy stored in a capacitor of capacitance \(C\) charged to potential \(V\) is:\[U = \frac{1}{2} C V^2\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values into the formula:\[U = \frac{1}{2} \times \left(12 \times 10^{-12}\text{ F}\right) \times (50\text{ V})^2 = 6 \times 10^{-12} \times 2500 = 15000 \times 10^{-12}\text{ J} = 1.5 \times 10^{-8}\text{ J}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units evaluate to \(\text{F}\cdot\text{V}^2 = \text{C}\cdot\text{V} = \text{J}\). The total stored energy is \(1.5 \times 10^{-8}\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q07 - Electric potential at dipole equatorial plane

questiontext.text: An electric dipole consists of two opposite charges of magnitude \(q = 2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}\) separated by a distance of \(2.0\text{ cm}\). What is the electrostatic potential at any point on its equatorial plane at a distance of \(15\text{ cm}\) from the center of the dipole?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: dipole charges \(+q = +2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}\) and \(-q = -2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}\), separation \(2a = 2.0\text{ cm}\), and distance of observation point from dipole center \(r = 15\text{ cm}\) on the equatorial plane.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Any point on the equatorial plane is equidistant from both the positive charge \(+q\) and the negative charge \(-q\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The electrostatic potential due to a dipole at a point \((r, \theta)\) is:\[V = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{p \cos\theta}{r^2}\]For any point on the equatorial plane, \(\theta = 90^\circ\). Alternatively, by superposition:\[V = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\frac{+q}{r_1} + \frac{-q}{r_2}\right)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Since \(r_1 = r_2\) on the equatorial perpendicular bisector:\[V = \frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\frac{1}{r_1} - \frac{1}{r_1}\right) = 0\text{ V}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The positive potential from the positive charge cancels identically with the negative potential from the negative charge. Hence, the electric potential is \(0\text{ V}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q08 - Zero potential point between two charges

questiontext.text: Two point charges \(q_1 = 5 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\) and \(q_2 = -3 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\) are located \(16\text{ cm}\) apart in air. At what distance from the positive charge \(q_1\) along the line segment joining the two charges is the electrostatic potential zero?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: positive charge \(q_1 = 5 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\), negative charge \(q_2 = -3 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\), and total separation \(d = 16\text{ cm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Let the point of zero potential lie on the line segment between the two charges at a distance \(x\) from \(q_1\). The distance from \(q_2\) is then \((d - x)\), where \(0 < x < d\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The net electrostatic potential is the scalar sum of the potentials from each point charge:\[V = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\frac{q_1}{x} + \frac{q_2}{d - x}\right) = 0\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Setting the sum to zero gives:\[\frac{q_1}{x} = -\frac{q_2}{d - x}\]Substitute \(q_1 = 5 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\) and \(q_2 = -3 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\):\[\frac{5}{x} = \frac{3}{16 - x}\]Cross-multiply and solve for \(x\):\[5(16 - x) = 3x \implies 80 - 5x = 3x \implies 8x = 80 \implies x = 10\text{ cm}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The calculated distance \(x = 10\text{ cm}\) is closer to the smaller magnitude charge (\(6\text{ cm}\) from \(-3 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\)), as physically expected for equalizing potentials of opposite signs. The distance is \(10\text{ cm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q09 - Potential at center of regular hexagon

questiontext.text: A regular hexagon of side length \(10\text{ cm}\) has an equal charge of \(5.0\ \mu\text{C}\) placed at each of its six vertices. Calculate the electrostatic potential at the geometric center of the hexagon. (Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: side of the regular hexagon \(a = 10\text{ cm} = 0.1\text{ m}\), charge at each vertex \(q = 5.0\ \mu\text{C} = 5.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}\), and number of vertices \(n = 6\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In a regular hexagon, the distance from each vertex to the geometric center is equal to the side length of the hexagon: \(r = a = 0.1\text{ m}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
By the principle of superposition, electrostatic potential is a scalar quantity, so the net potential at the center is the sum of potentials due to all 6 charges:\[V = \sum_{i=1}^{6} V_i = 6 \times \left(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q}{r}\right)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the numerical values:\[V = 6 \times \left(9 \times 10^9 \times \frac{5.0 \times 10^{-6}}{0.1}\right) = 6 \times \left(\frac{45000}{0.1}\right) = 6 \times \left(4.5 \times 10^5\right) = 2.7 \times 10^6\text{ V}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
All six charges are positive, so their scalar potentials reinforce each other constructively. The total potential is \(2.7 \times 10^6\text{ V}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q10 - Electrostatic potential along short dipole axis

questiontext.text: A short electric dipole has a dipole moment of \(1.6 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}\). What is the electrostatic potential at an axial point at a distance of \(0.12\text{ m}\) from the center of the dipole on the side of the positive charge?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: dipole moment \(p = 1.6 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}\), distance along the axis \(r = 0.12\text{ m}\), and angle with dipole axis \(\theta = 0^\circ\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Assume a short dipole approximation where the separation between dipole charges is much smaller than the distance \(r\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The electrostatic potential of a short dipole at distance \(r\) and angle \(\theta\) is given by:\[V = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{p \cos\theta}{r^2}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For an axial point on the positive side, \(\cos 0^\circ = 1\):\[V = \left(9 \times 10^9\right) \times \frac{1.6 \times 10^{-9}}{(0.12)^2} = \frac{14.4}{0.0144} = 1000\text{ V}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The inverse-square distance dependence gives a positive potential of \(1000\text{ V}\) along the dipole axis on the positive side.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q11 - Work done rotating dipole in electric field

questiontext.text: An electric dipole of dipole moment \(2.0 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}\) is initially aligned parallel to a uniform electric field of magnitude \(1.0 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}\). How much work must be done by an external agent to rotate the dipole through \(180^\circ\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: dipole moment \(p = 2.0 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}\), uniform electric field \(E = 1.0 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}\), initial angle \(\theta_1 = 0^\circ\), and final angle \(\theta_2 = 180^\circ\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The rotation is carried out very slowly without changing the kinetic energy of the dipole.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The potential energy of a dipole in an external field is \(U(\theta) = -p E \cos\theta\). The work done by an external agent is:\[W = U(\theta_2) - U(\theta_1) = p E(\cos\theta_1 - \cos\theta_2)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the known values into the expression:\[W = \left(2.0 \times 10^{-8}\right) \times \left(1.0 \times 10^4\right) \times \left[\cos(0^\circ) - \cos(180^\circ)\right]\]Since \(\cos(0^\circ) = 1\) and \(\cos(180^\circ) = -1\):\[W = 2.0 \times 10^{-4} \times [1 - (-1)] = 2.0 \times 10^{-4} \times 2 = 4.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ J}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Rotating against the restoring torque of the field from stable equilibrium requires positive external work. The work done is \(4.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q12 - Separation between two planar equipotential surfaces

questiontext.text: The uniform electric field between two parallel equipotential surfaces is \(500\text{ V/m}\). If the potential difference between the surfaces is \(20\text{ V}\), what is the perpendicular distance between them?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: potential difference between equipotential surfaces \(\Delta V = 20\text{ V}\), and uniform electric field strength \(E = 500\text{ V/m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The electric field is uniform and directed perpendicular to the equipotential surfaces in the direction of decreasing potential.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The relation between uniform electric field and potential gradient is:\[E = \frac{\Delta V}{\Delta r}\]where \(\Delta r\) is the perpendicular separation between the equipotential surfaces.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Solve for \(\Delta r\):\[\Delta r = \frac{\Delta V}{E} = \frac{20\text{ V}}{500\text{ V/m}} = 0.04\text{ m}\]Convert meters to centimeters:\[\Delta r = 0.04 \times 100\text{ cm} = 4.0\text{ cm}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The units \(\text{V} / (\text{V/m}) = \text{m}\), which yields \(4.0\text{ cm}\). The perpendicular distance between the surfaces is \(4.0\text{ cm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q13 - Potential inside a charged spherical conductor

questiontext.text: A spherical conductor of radius \(12\text{ cm}\) has a charge of \(1.6 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}\) distributed uniformly over its surface. What is the electric potential at a point located \(6.0\text{ cm}\) from the center of the sphere? (Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: radius of spherical conductor \(R = 12\text{ cm} = 0.12\text{ m}\), surface charge \(q = 1.6 \times 10^{-7}\text{ C}\), and observation distance \(r = 6.0\text{ cm} = 0.06\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
For a conducting sphere in electrostatic equilibrium, the electric field inside is zero everywhere: \(E = 0\) for \(r < R\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Because \(E = -\frac{dV}{dr} = 0\) inside the conductor, the potential \(V\) is constant throughout the entire volume of the conductor and equals the potential at the surface:\[V_{\text{inside}} = V_{\text{surface}} = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q}{R}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given numbers:\[V = \left(9 \times 10^9\right) \times \frac{1.6 \times 10^{-7}}{0.12} = \frac{1440}{0.12} = 1.2 \times 10^4\text{ V}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The potential inside does not depend on \(r\) as long as \(r \le R\). The electric potential at the point is \(1.2 \times 10^4\text{ V}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q14 - Potential energy of three equal charges

questiontext.text: Three identical point charges of \(+2.0\ \mu\text{C}\) each are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side \(0.50\text{ m}\). What is the total electrostatic potential energy of the system? (Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: three equal charges \(q_1 = q_2 = q_3 = q = 2.0\ \mu\text{C} = 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}\), and side length of equilateral triangle \(r = 0.50\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The potential energy of the system is the sum of interaction energies over all unique pairs of charges: \(\binom{3}{2} = 3\) distinct pairs.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The total electrostatic potential energy is given by:\[U = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\frac{q_1 q_2}{r_{12}} + \frac{q_2 q_3}{r_{23}} + \frac{q_3 q_1}{r_{31}}\right) = 3 \times \left(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q^2}{r}\right)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the pair potential energy:\[U_{\text{pair}} = \left(9 \times 10^9\right) \times \frac{\left(2.0 \times 10^{-6}\right)^2}{0.50} = \frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 4.0 \times 10^{-12}}{0.50} = \frac{0.036}{0.50} = 0.072\text{ J}\]Multiply by 3 for the three pairs:\[U = 3 \times 0.072\text{ J} = 0.216\text{ J}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since all charges have like signs, the mutual potential energy is strictly positive. The total potential energy is \(0.216\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q15 - Work done moving test charge in dipole

questiontext.text: Two point charges \(+3.0\ \mu\text{C}\) and \(-3.0\ \mu\text{C}\) are fixed at points \(A(0, 0, -2.0\text{ cm})\) and \(B(0, 0, 2.0\text{ cm})\) respectively. How much work is done by an external agent in moving a test charge of \(5.0\ \mu\text{C}\) from point \(C(4.0\text{ cm}, 0, 0)\) to point \(D(0, 6.0\text{ cm}, 0)\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: dipole charges \(+q\) at \((0, 0, -2.0\text{ cm})\) and \(-q\) at \((0, 0, 2.0\text{ cm})\), test charge \(q_0 = 5.0\ \mu\text{C}\), initial position \(C(4.0\text{ cm}, 0, 0)\), and final position \(D(0, 6.0\text{ cm}, 0)\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The dipole lies entirely along the z-axis with its center at the origin \((0, 0, 0)\). The xy-plane (\(z = 0\)) is the equatorial plane of the dipole.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The electrostatic potential at any point in the equatorial plane of an electric dipole is zero:\[V(x, y, 0) = 0\text{ V}\]The work done in moving a charge between two points is \(W = q_0(V_D - V_C)\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Both points \(C(4.0\text{ cm}, 0, 0)\) and \(D(0, 6.0\text{ cm}, 0)\) have \(z = 0\), meaning both lie in the equatorial plane:\[V_C = 0\text{ V},\quad V_D = 0\text{ V}\]Hence, the potential difference is:\[\Delta V = V_D - V_C = 0\text{ V}\]Therefore:\[W = q_0 \times 0 = 0\text{ J}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Because electrostatic forces are conservative and the initial and final potentials are identical, the work done is \(0\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q16 - Charge on capacitor with dielectric and battery

questiontext.text: A parallel plate capacitor with capacitance \(C_0 = 10\text{ pF}\) is connected to a \(100\text{ V}\) battery. While the battery remains connected, a dielectric slab of dielectric constant \(K = 6.0\) is inserted to fill the entire space between the plates. What is the new charge on the capacitor?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: initial capacitance \(C_0 = 10\text{ pF} = 10 \times 10^{-12}\text{ F}\), supply voltage \(V = 100\text{ V}\), and dielectric constant \(K = 6.0\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Because the battery remains connected, the potential difference between the plates remains constant at \(V = 100\text{ V}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
When a dielectric of dielectric constant \(K\) fills the capacitor, the new capacitance becomes:\[C' = K C_0 = 6.0 \times 10\text{ pF} = 60\text{ pF}\]The new charge stored on the plates is \(Q' = C' V\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the charge:\[Q' = \left(60 \times 10^{-12}\text{ F}\right) \times 100\text{ V} = 6000 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C} = 6.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C} = 6.0\text{ nC}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The charge increases by a factor of \(K = 6\) from its initial value of \(1.0\text{ nC}\). Thus, the new charge is \(6.0\text{ nC}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q17 - Potential difference with dielectric and disconnected battery

questiontext.text: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance \(10\text{ pF}\) is charged by a \(100\text{ V}\) power supply. The power supply is then disconnected, after which a dielectric slab of dielectric constant \(K = 5.0\) is inserted between the plates. What is the potential difference across the capacitor now?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: initial capacitance \(C_0 = 10\text{ pF}\), initial potential difference \(V_0 = 100\text{ V}\), and dielectric constant \(K = 5.0\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Because the battery is disconnected before inserting the dielectric slab, the electric charge on the isolated plates is conserved: \(Q = Q_0\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The capacitance increases to \(C = K C_0\). The new potential difference across the plates is:\[V = \frac{Q}{C} = \frac{Q_0}{K C_0} = \frac{V_0}{K}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the known numerical values:\[V = \frac{100\text{ V}}{5.0} = 20\text{ V}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The dielectric polarizes in the electric field, reducing the internal electric field and consequently reducing the potential difference by a factor of \(K\). The new potential difference is \(20\text{ V}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q18 - Electrostatic energy density in electric field

questiontext.text: The uniform electric field between the plates of a parallel plate air capacitor has a magnitude of \(3.0 \times 10^4\text{ V/m}\). Taking \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2\text{N}^{-1}\text{m}^{-2}\), what is the electrostatic energy density in the region between the plates?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: electric field strength \(E = 3.0 \times 10^4\text{ V/m}\), and permittivity of free space \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ F/m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The medium between the plates is air/vacuum with relative permittivity \(\varepsilon_r = 1\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The electrostatic energy density (energy per unit volume) stored in an electric field is given by:\[u = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given numbers:\[u = \frac{1}{2} \times \left(8.85 \times 10^{-12}\right) \times \left(3.0 \times 10^4\right)^2 = 0.5 \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 9.0 \times 10^8\]Multiply out the terms:\[u = 4.425 \times 10^{-12} \times 9.0 \times 10^8 = 39.825 \times 10^{-4} = 3.98 \times 10^{-3}\text{ J/m}^3\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The resulting units are \(\text{F/m} \cdot (\text{V/m})^2 = \text{J/m}^3\). The electrostatic energy density is \(3.98 \times 10^{-3}\text{ J/m}^3\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q19 - Voltage distribution across series connected capacitors

questiontext.text: Two capacitors of capacitances \(3.0\ \mu\text{F}\) and \(6.0\ \mu\text{F}\) are connected in series across a \(120\text{ V}\) DC voltage source. What is the potential difference across the \(3.0\ \mu\text{F}\) capacitor?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: series capacitors \(C_1 = 3.0\ \mu\text{F}\) and \(C_2 = 6.0\ \mu\text{F}\), and total source voltage \(V = 120\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In a series combination, each capacitor holds the same charge \(Q\). The total voltage divides inversely proportional to capacitance: \(V = V_1 + V_2\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The equivalent capacitance is:\[C_{eq} = \frac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2}\]The voltage across \(C_1\) is:\[V_1 = \frac{Q}{C_1} = V \left(\frac{C_2}{C_1 + C_2}\right)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values:\[V_1 = 120\text{ V} \times \left(\frac{6.0\ \mu\text{F}}{3.0\ \mu\text{F} + 6.0\ \mu\text{F}}\right) = 120 \times \frac{6.0}{9.0} = 120 \times \frac{2}{3} = 80\text{ V}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The smaller capacitor develops the larger share of the voltage (\(V_1 = 80\text{ V}\), \(V_2 = 40\text{ V}\), summing to \(120\text{ V}\)). Thus, the potential difference across the \(3.0\ \mu\text{F}\) capacitor is \(80\text{ V}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q20 - Total charge drawn by parallel capacitors

questiontext.text: Two capacitors of capacitances \(4.0\ \mu\text{F}\) and \(8.0\ \mu\text{F}\) are connected in parallel across a \(20\text{ V}\) battery. What is the total electric charge drawn from the battery by this combination?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: capacitances in parallel \(C_1 = 4.0\ \mu\text{F}\) and \(C_2 = 8.0\ \mu\text{F}\), connected across voltage \(V = 20\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In a parallel connection, both capacitors experience the full battery voltage \(V\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The equivalent capacitance of the parallel combination is:\[C_p = C_1 + C_2\]The total charge supplied by the battery is:\[Q = C_p V = (C_1 + C_2)V\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the numerical values:\[C_p = 4.0\ \mu\text{F} + 8.0\ \mu\text{F} = 12.0\ \mu\text{F}\]\[Q = 12.0\ \mu\text{F} \times 20\text{ V} = 240\ \mu\text{C}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking individual charges: \(Q_1 = 4.0 \times 20 = 80\ \mu\text{C}\) and \(Q_2 = 8.0 \times 20 = 160\ \mu\text{C}\). Their sum is \(80 + 160 = 240\ \mu\text{C}\). The total charge drawn is \(240\ \mu\text{C}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q21 - Equivalent capacitance of series parallel network

questiontext.text: Two capacitors of capacitances \(6.0\ \mu\text{F}\) and \(12.0\ \mu\text{F}\) are connected in parallel. This combination is then connected in series with a third capacitor of capacitance \(9.0\ \mu\text{F}\). What is the equivalent capacitance of the entire circuit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: parallel branch containing \(C_1 = 6.0\ \mu\text{F}\) and \(C_2 = 12.0\ \mu\text{F}\), in series with \(C_3 = 9.0\ \mu\text{F}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
First simplify the parallel sub-network, then combine the resulting capacitance in series with the third capacitor.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The equivalent capacitance of the parallel branch is:\[C_p = C_1 + C_2 = 6.0\ \mu\text{F} + 12.0\ \mu\text{F} = 18.0\ \mu\text{F}\]The overall equivalent capacitance \(C_{eq}\) of \(C_p\) in series with \(C_3\) is:\[C_{eq} = \frac{C_p \times C_3}{C_p + C_3}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the computed values:\[C_{eq} = \frac{18.0 \times 9.0}{18.0 + 9.0} = \frac{162.0}{27.0} = 6.0\ \mu\text{F}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The overall capacitance \(6.0\ \mu\text{F}\) is less than the series component \(9.0\ \mu\text{F}\), which satisfies the properties of series reduction. The equivalent capacitance is \(6.0\ \mu\text{F}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q22 - Maximum operating voltage before dielectric breakdown

questiontext.text: A dielectric medium has a dielectric constant \(K = 4.0\) and a dielectric breakdown strength of \(2.0 \times 10^7\text{ V/m}\). If this dielectric is used in a parallel plate capacitor of plate separation \(0.25\text{ mm}\), what is the maximum operating voltage that can be applied across the plates so that the internal electric field does not exceed \(10\%\) of the dielectric strength?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: dielectric breakdown strength \(E_{\text{break}} = 2.0 \times 10^7\text{ V/m}\), safety limit factor \(= 10\% = 0.10\), and plate separation \(d = 0.25\text{ mm} = 0.25 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The electric field between parallel plates is assumed uniform, so \(V = E d\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The permissible electric field is:\[E_{\text{safe}} = 0.10 \times E_{\text{break}}\]The maximum operating voltage is:\[V_{\max} = E_{\text{safe}} \times d\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Compute \(E_{\text{safe}}\):\[E_{\text{safe}} = 0.10 \times \left(2.0 \times 10^7\text{ V/m}\right) = 2.0 \times 10^6\text{ V/m}\]Now calculate \(V_{\max}\):\[V_{\max} = \left(2.0 \times 10^6\text{ V/m}\right) \times \left(0.25 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}\right) = 0.50 \times 10^3\text{ V} = 500\text{ V}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units check: \(\text{V/m} \times \text{m} = \text{V}\). The safe operating voltage is \(500\text{ V}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q23 - Work done changing capacitor plate separation

questiontext.text: An isolated parallel plate air capacitor of capacitance \(2.0\ \mu\text{F}\) carries a charge of \(4.0\ \mu\text{C}\). If the plate separation is doubled while keeping the capacitor isolated, how much mechanical work is done by the external agent against the electrostatic attractive force?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Given: initial capacitance \(C_1 = 2.0\ \mu\text{F} = 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F}\), charge \(Q = 4.0\ \mu\text{C} = 4.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C}\), and separation is doubled (\(d_2 = 2 d_1\)).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Because the capacitor is isolated, its charge \(Q\) remains constant throughout the mechanical displacement.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
